42671476.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Primary aim was to evaluate whether presence of osteoarthritis (OA), as assessed by ordinal grading on whole-body computed tomography (CT), is associated with 68 Ga fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) positron emission tomography (PET) tracer uptake as a measure of fibroblastic activation. Secondary aim was to evaluate whether OA disease severity is positively correlated with increased tracer uptake and to evaluate reliability. MATERIAL AND METHODS: In a retrospective study design, patients who had undergone 68 Ga-FAPI PET-CT for a spectrum of clinical reasons were included. Whole-body CT was assessed for OA using the OsteoArthritis Computed Tomography-Score in multiple joints and the spine. Maximum standard uptake value (SUVmax) was determined correspondingly. Logistic regression and correlation analyses were used to describe associations between structural OA and 68 Ga-FAPI PET activity. RESULTS: Fifty-four patients were included. Presence of OA in the acromioclavicular joints (ACJ) was associated with odds of SUVmax being in the highest tertile. 42656957.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a major diagnostic challenge in emergency medicine. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is the gold standard but is frequently overused. The modified Wells Score (mWS) estimates pre-test probability and may reduce inappropriate imaging at triage. We evaluated the concordance between mWS and CTPA-confirmed PE in a tertiary emergency department. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed all patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE over 24 months. As all patients had already undergone CTPA, this design reflects concordance within an imaging-selected cohort, not triage performance. mWS values were assigned by consensus between two readers, blinded to CTPA results; D-dimer was not incorporated. AUC was computed from the full ordinal mWS range; sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV were calculated at the conventional mWS ≥ 4 threshold. Spearman's correlation assessed the mWS-PE severity association. RESULTS: Among 691 patients, 103 (14.9%) had CTPA-confirmed PE. At mWS ≥ 4, sensitivity was 86.4%, specificity 98.6%, AUC 0.943 (95% CI: 0.91-0.97). The Youden index identified mWS ≥ 3 as optimal (sensitivity 89.3%, specificity 95.7%); ≥ 4 was r

42576970.abstract: Recanalization after intravenous thrombolysis remains incomplete in many stroke patients, highlighting the need for standardized preclinical methods to evaluate thrombolytic therapies. We developed a rat systemic embolization model combined with high-resolution micro-fluoroscopy enabling direct, real-time, and quantitative assessment of thrombolysis in vivo. Human fibrin-based BaSO₄ labeled clots were introduced into the abdominal aorta (three clots/animal) to assess alteplase (rtPA) efficacy at doses of 0.9 and 5 mg/kg/h. Micro-CT imaging served as a reference modality. Micro-fluoroscopy continuously visualized clot dissolution, detecting a mean of two clots per animal. Thrombolysis resulted in a dose-dependent reduction in clot area (mean ± SD; -46 ± 26% and -81 ± 22% for 0.9 and 5 mg/kg/h rtPA, respectively, versus -21 ± 14% in controls). Measurement reliability was high (ICC = 0.89), and concordance with micro-CT supported concurrent validity. 42564513.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to validate the diagnostic value of kinetic heterogeneity (KH) across multiple cohorts and to develop a nomogram integrating KH, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), and key morphological and clinical features for preoperative discrimination between benign and malignant breast masses. METHODS: This retrospective study included 501 female patients with 541 confirmed breast mass lesions. Training (n = 280) and internal validation (n = 119) cohorts were collected (2018-2019). Temporal validation (n = 101, 2024) and independent test cohorts (n = 41, 2025-2026), from a different scanner system) were also included. KH was computed using voxel-wise time-intensity curve analysis. Independent predictors were identified using logistic regression to construct a nomogram. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis, and compared with KH-, ADC-, and combined models. RESULTS: Age, lesion margin, ADC, and KH were independent predictors. Researchers have begun to develop and continue to innovate Molecular & Imaging processes, called Liquid Biopsies, that are now being used to assess health risk factors associated with PC, by sampling macro-molecules from various biological liquids. 42535878.abstract: This study evaluates the association between baseline left ventricular (LV) peak strain dispersion (PSD) and 3-to-5-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD). This single-center retrospective cohort study screened 586 adult patients undergoing MHD at a tertiary renal unit between January 2018 and December 2020, with follow-up through June 2024. Patients were stratified by baseline PSD at the prespecified cutoff of ≥65 ms. One-to-one propensity score matching (nearest neighbor, caliper: 0.02) using 24 covariates was applied to minimize confounding. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)-a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, hospitalization for heart failure, nonfatal stroke and sustained ventricular arrhythmia. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves, matched-pair robust Cox proportional hazards models and competing-risk sensitivity analyses. After matching, 336 patients (168 per group) were analyzed, with excellent covariate balance (all standardized mean differences <0.10). Over a median follow-up of 46.8 mo

42491319.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preoperative differentiation of pulmonary nodules into preinvasive (AAH/AIS), minimally invasive (MIA) and invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC) subtypes is vital for clinical decision-making, but conventional radiomics lacks biological interpretability and reproducibility. This study proposed a Moran's I-driven habitat radiomics approach to evaluate the temporal stability of invasiveness risk assessment on serial CT. METHODS: A total of 614 patients from two centers were enrolled, including a training set (n = 400), an internal validation set (n = 104), and an independent external testing set (n = 110). Notably, the external set comprised patients with serial longitudinal CT scans (preoperative, 3-, 6-, and 12-month) to validate temporal generalizability. Local Moran's I partitioned tumors into four habitats by spatial autocorrelation. Feature reproducibility was verified via image perturbation, and an optimal combined model was built with robust habitat features and compared with conventional radiomics. 42478222.abstract: Maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients are at high risk of valve calcification (VC) and cardiomegaly, defined as cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) ≥0.5. CTR is a widely used indicator of volume overload and left ventricular dysfunction and predicts adverse cardiovascular outcomes. However, the combined prognostic impact of VC and high CTR on cardiovascular mortality remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective, single-center, exploratory study enrolling MHD patients from October to December, 2018. Patients were stratified into four groups based on VC and CTR (<0.5 or ≥0.5). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and the Kaplan-Meier method were used to evaluate risks and cumulative incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), cardiovascular mortality, and overall mortality among groups. Of 312 MHD patients, 37 had no VC with CTR <0.5, 47 had no VC with CTR ≥0.5, 96 had VC with CTR <0.5, and 132 had VC with CTR ≥0.5. Compared to MHD patients without VC and CTR <0.5, those with VC and CTR ≥0.5 had higher risks of MACEs, cardiovascular mortality and overall mortality (adjusted hazard ratios: 4.174, 6.426, and 4.031; 95% confidence intervals: 1.766-9.868, 1.503-27.48, an

42444639.abstract: Prohibitive costs associated with high-field MRI systems have resulted in reduced access in resource-limited areas with consequential healthcare inequities. This has renewed interest in purposefully designed low-field (LF) systems that, despite inherently lower signal-to-noise ratios, have advantages in terms of cost, portability, and accessibility. This pilot study successfully translated a previously developed LF (0.05 T) MRI canine cadaver brain protocol for in vivo application and compared the acquired images with paired 1.5 T images from 21 different canine patients. The visibility of 15 anatomic features was ordinarily scored (scale 1-3) on transverse T1-weighted post-contrast (21/21 patients) and T2-weighted (17/21 patients) sequences. Lateral ventricles were easily visualized (89.3%-100% scored 3/3) across all sequence‒system combinations, with T2-weighted sequences also providing good identification of the mesencephalic aqueduct (56.3%-100%), fourth ventricle (77.1%-100%), and thalamus (68.8%-100%). 42443716.abstract: Although cardiovascular complications are the most common cause of morbidity and mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD), the detection of subclinical cardiorenal remodeling is still limited. This is a single-center, exploratory observational study of 127 patients with CKD of various etiologies (hypertensive nephropathy, diabetic nephropathy and chronic glomerulonephritis) and 30 healthy controls. In addition to transthoracic echocardiography at rest and after exercise, biomarkers of podocyte injury (urinary nephrin), fibrosis (urinary type IV collagen and serum galectin-3), cardiac wall stress (serum NT-proBNP) and renal filtration/cardiovascular risk integration (serum cystatin C) were assessed. Biomarker abnormalities were consistent across all CKD groups, even in the absence of overt heart-failure symptoms and preserved ejection fraction. Urinary nephrin and type IV collagen were significantly increased, as were galectin-3 and NT-proBNP concentrations. All CKD groups had resting E/e' values above the normal range and these values were further elevated following exercise. 42440417.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of using the free-breathing (FB) radial stack-of-stars fast spoiled gradient recalled-echo (FSPGR) sequence as an alternative to the conventional breath-hold (BH) FSPGR sequence for hepatic T1 mapping across the clinical range of body mass index (BMI). METHODS: From 07/2024 to 10/2024, 75 participants who underwent both FB and BH FSPGR were analyzed. Participants were stratified into 3 BMI groups. BH IDEAL IQ was also collected to enable PDFF to be evaluated. Quantitative assessments involved whole-liver T1 estimates, volumes, PDFF and the ratio of |T1liver-T1sat|/T1liver. A five-point Likert scale was used for qualitative assessments. RESULTS: The ratios of |T1liver-T1sat|/T1 liver in FB T1 mapping were higher than those of BH T1 mapping in the overall population and obese group (p both < 0.05). No significant difference was found in liver T1 estimates in patients with BH failure between sequences (p＞0.05). FB T1 mapping outperformed BH in artifact scores for the obese group (p = 0.015). 42411251.abstract: AIM/INTRODUCTION: Adenosine pharmacological stress is commonly used for the detection of ischemia by myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) using radiotracers and gated single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) imaging. Recently, a phenomenon, splenic switch-off (SSO), has been observed where reduced perfusion to the spleen occurs after adenosine, suggesting an adequate effect of adenosine on the heart. The aim of the study is to evaluate the SSO effect in adenosine stress 99m Tc tetrofosmin MPI studies using semiquantitative analysis of SPECT/CT data. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seventeen adenosine MPI studies were selected. Each study included stress and rest, which were reoriented in short, horizontal, and vertical long axes. Also, data were reconstructed in the body transaxial, coronal, and sagittal planes. In the resulting images, the spleen was identified on the CT component, and regions of interest were drawn on the spleen, thoracic vertebra, and myocardium. 42376195.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To clarify the characteristics of virtual non-contrast (VNC) images generated from each phase of triphasic dynamic liver computed tomography (CT) using second-generation dual-layer spectral CT (DLCT). METHODS: A second-generation DLCT system, the Spectral CT 7500, was used for the three-phase dynamic liver CT examination of 31 patients from August 2024 to February 2025. VNC images were generated from the arterial phase (AP), portal venous phase (PVP), and equilibrium phase (EP). For a quantitative evaluation, the agreement between liver parenchymal CT values from the VNC images created from the three phases and the true non-contrast (TNC) images was assessed by a Bland-Altman analysis (pre-set clinical limit: ±10 HU). In the qualitative evaluation, five parameters (vascular remnants, visibility of the portal and hepatic veins, image noise, image distortion, and overall image quality) were assessed using a four-point rating scale. RESULTS: In the quantitative analysis, the mean difference (bias) between the VNC and TNC images was -2.19 for AP, -0.14 for PVP, and -2.11 HU for EP, and the 95% limits of agreement were within the pre-set clinical limit for all phases. 42376199.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive imaging techniques such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offer advantages over repeated biopsies for assessing tumor characteristics, though histological and molecular analysis remain the diagnostic gold standard. Since P53 expression is an important prognostic factor linked to the histopathological patterns of endometrial cancer (EC), using MRI-derived indices to distinguish between TP53-mutated (P53abn) and non-P53abn subtypes is clinically practical. This study aimed to determine the predictive value of MRI-based markers, especially apparent diffusion coefficients (ADC), for differentiating P53abn and non-P53abn subtypes in patients with EC. METHODS: This retrospective study was performed on 115 patients with known EC. All MR imaging studies were performed on 1.5 T MR imaging units. The presence of p53abn subtype was determined by immunohistochemical staining (IHC). Data were analyzed using R version 4.4.1. RESULTS: A statistically significant difference was observed in mean ADC values between patients with and without p53abn by IHC, with notably lower ADC values in the P53abn group. 42999552.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The predictive value of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) for extraprostatic extension (EPE) in prostate cancer remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: We assessed whether adding PSMA PET/CT to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical factors improves side-specific EPE prediction. METHODS: Patients undergoing PSMA PET/CT and MRI before radical prostatectomy were analysed retrospectively. The endpoint was side-specific EPE (≥pT3a). Predictors were selected by backward elimination, and the final nomogram was fitted using generalised estimating equations to account for clustering of lobes within patients. Discrimination, calibration, and net benefit were assessed, with external validation in an independent single-centre cohort. RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: Development and validation cohorts included 801 and 287 lobes. 42993636.abstract: BACKGROUND: Management of a degenerative meniscal tear (DMT) or symptoms consistent with early knee osteoarthritis (OA) frequently deviates from international clinical practice guidelines, which recommend education and exercise as first-line treatments and strongly advise against arthroscopic partial meniscectomy. There is a need for implementation strategies to support the uptake of evidence-based care. METHODS: A systematic, four-step intervention development process was used to guide development of a multi-faceted implementation intervention targeting both individuals with a DMT or early knee OA and their general practitioners (GPs). The process integrated behavioural theory, stakeholder perspectives and evidence on intervention effectiveness. Target behaviours were identified through a literature review and stakeholder consultation. Previously conducted qualitative interviews with 17 GPs and 11 people with DMT were re-analysed and mapped to the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) to identify behavioural barriers and enablers to the targeted behaviours. Behaviour change techniques (BCTs) and intervention components were then selected to address these determinants. Stakeholder in

42992227.abstract: Emulsion gels combine the kinetic stability of emulsions with the structural integrity of gels by immobilizing oil droplets in a three-dimensional network, thereby limiting conventional emulsion instabilities and supporting delivery of hydrophobic bioactives. Pectin, an abundant and food-approved acidic heteropolysaccharide, is an attractive matrix because of its amphiphilicity and tunable gelation. A critical synthesis focused specifically on pectin-based emulsion gels-covering formation mechanisms, interfacial behaviour, multiscale structure-property relationships and application prospects-is still limited. This review examines preparation, interfacial and gelation mechanisms, multiscale characterization, key influencing factors and translational potential, with emphasis on how pectin molecular architecture (degree of methoxylation (DM), rhamnogalacturonan-I (RG-I) domains and proteinaceous moieties) shapes colloidal behaviour. By identifying current limitations and open questions, it aims to support more rational design of pectin-based emulsion gels for food structuring, nutraceutical delivery and related soft-matter uses.

42990978.abstract: PURPOSE: The purpose of this case report is to describe a rare case of retained orbital brachytherapy seeds implanted during infancy and identified in an older adult undergoing neurocognitive evaluation. It highlights a multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and management. OBSERVATIONS: An 85-year-old man presented for removal of radiopaque periocular foreign bodies prior to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for a neurocognitive workup. The patient reported undergoing "seed placement" radiation therapy to the right orbital region at 18 months of age in Scotland for a superior right orbital mass, suspected to be a capillary hemangioma. Computed tomography revealed two discrete radiopaque foreign bodies in the superior right orbit and right medial nasal soft tissue. Multidisciplinary evaluation with ocular oncology and radiation safety suggested that the foreign bodies were retained casings from historical radon-222 brachytherapy seeds. Preoperative and intraoperative assessments demonstrated no detectable residual radioactivity, and the foreign bodies were removed successfully, allowing the patient to proceed with MRI. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPORTANCE: This case highlights the importance

42990956.abstract: Oral probiotics face viability challenges during processing, storage, and gastrointestinal transit. This critical review provides a unified analytical framework for polysaccharide-based conjugated probiotic encapsulation, bridging synthesis chemistry, delivery mechanisms, and industrial feasibility. Covalent modification and network-forming routes, including Maillard glycation, chemical crosslinking, enzymatic crosslinking, radical-mediated grafting, and thiol-based functionalization, are compared with non-covalent assembly and energy-assisted processing in terms of network architecture, thermal resistance, and scalability. Colon-targeted release mechanisms, including pH-responsive swelling, enzymatic degradation, microbiota fermentation, and multi-stimuli architectures, are critically evaluated. Practical applicability in commercial matrices like yogurt, kefir, honey, and ice cream is discussed alongside processing and regulatory considerations. While conjugated matrices offer superior gastric protection and controllable release, critical gaps remain in release kinetics, long-term storage data, residual crosslinker safety, and strain-specific variability. 42990772.abstract: PURPOSE: To report a case of medulloepithelioma treated with palladium-103 (103Pd) plaque brachytherapy, followed by adjunctive continuous periodic intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, highlighting a novel combined strategy for tumor control and management of its neovascular complications. OBSERVATIONS: A 9-year-old male presented with a ciliary body mass causing anterior displacement of the iris and iris neovascularization in the right eye. Initial tumor dimensions were 8 × 8 mm in basal diameters and 3.9 mm in thickness. Aspiration cutter-assisted biopsy was used to confirm the diagnosis of medulloepithelioma. Treatment involved temporary placement of a 14-mm 103Pd plaque, which irradiated the tumor's apex to 101.4 Gy (Gy) over 7 days. Despite tumor control, progressive iris neovascularization with secondary angle-closure glaucoma was managed by continuous periodic intravitreal anti-VEGF pharmacotherapy and two peripheral iridotomies. At 18 months post-plaque brachytherapy, a posterior subcapsular cataract developed that required extraction with intraocular lens placement. 42985687.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the distribution of central subfield thickness (CST) measured by spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) in a longitudinal cohort of Ebola virus-seronegative individuals in Liberia. DESIGN: Longitudinal cohort study. METHODS: Close contacts of Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors enrolled in the PREVAIL III Eye Study in Monrovia, Liberia underwent comprehensive ophthalmic examinations and macular imaging with Cirrus 5000 SD-OCT over five annual study visits. Prior Ebola virus infection was assessed using anti-Ebola virus glycoprotein IgG serology, and seropositive close contacts were excluded. CST measurements and descriptive statistics were analyzed longitudinally. In a post hoc analysis, participants with uveitis or retinal pathology were excluded from analyses characterizing retinal thickness in otherwise healthy eyes. Statistical analyses were conducted using R. RESULTS: Among 644 seronegative close contacts who underwent baseline ophthalmic evaluation, 181 (28.1%) had complete CST measurements in at least one eye at baseline, increasing to 548 of 594 (92.3%) at the subsequent annual visit and 404 of 407 (99.3%) at the final study visit. 42985552.abstract: Urine sediment (uSed) has often been treated as a residual pellet of urinalysis. Here, we reframe it as a biosource for molecular diagnosis in genitourinary (GU) cancer, yet its promise lies less in the molecules it contains than in the methods that make them interpretable. uSed carries tumor-derived DNA, RNA, proteins, and metabolites that capture genetic, epigenetic, transcriptional, proteomic, and metabolic alterations, enabling early detection, risk stratification, therapeutic monitoring, and minimal residual disease surveillance. Its molecular cargo determines biological reach, whereas analytical methods determine the reliability of clinical readouts. This Materials-to-Methods distinction is essential because the field remains rich in discovery but poor in validation: high diagnostic accuracy is frequently reported, yet few uSed assays are prospective, externally validated, or shown to change clinical management. We therefore synthesize uSed as a distinct urine fraction, separate from whole urine, cell-free supernatant, and extracellular vesicles, and evaluate how pre-analytical variability, analytical rigor, and post-analytical evidence grading determine whether molecular sig

42985525.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Risk-based tools to guide care after percutaneous kidney biopsy (PKB) remain limited. We developed a simple preadmission risk score to predict post-PKB bleeding and support same-day discharge decisions, leveraging Japan's routine inpatient observation practice. METHODS: This retrospective study included 78,817 adults undergoing native PKB, using a nationwide Japanese inpatient database (2016-2021). Risk factors for early hemostatic intervention, defined as blood transfusion or surgical or interventional hemostasis within 6 days after PKB, were evaluated using logistic and L2-penalized multinomial logistic regressions. The fitted coefficients for day 0 were discretized to develop the Kidney biopsy Bleeding Index for Triage (K-BIT), using readily obtainable prebiopsy clinical variables. The scoring was internally validated using a held-out test cohort from the same dataset. RESULTS: The overall bleeding rate was 1.46%. Compared with chronic glomerulonephritis, bleeding risk was higher in acute kidney injury (odds ratio [OR], 10.9; 95% confidence interval [CI], 8.55-13.9) and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (OR, 6.67; 95% CI 5.48-8.12). 42985341.abstract: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE: Pediatric anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) aneurysms are rare; radiation-associated dissecting lesions require exclusion without compromising brainstem or cerebellar perforators. CLINICAL PRESENTATION: A 13-year-old boy developed a progressively enlarging right AICA a2 dissecting aneurysm after cranial irradiation for pineal nongerminomatous germ cell tumor. Because direct clipping or isolated parent vessel occlusion was considered high risk, he underwent occipital artery-AICA a3 bypass followed by endovascular coil embolization in a single hybrid session. Dual arterial access enabled transradial vertebral artery treatment and transfemoral angiographic bypass assessment. Postoperative MRI showed a small transient cerebellar ischemic lesion that resolved within 2 weeks. At 2 months, the patient was neurologically intact with patent bypass and no aneurysm recurrence. CONCLUSION: Hybrid occipital artery-AICA bypass followed by endovascular embolization is a feasible flow-preserving option for selected pediatric AICA aneurysms requiring distal perfusion preservation.

42978842.abstract: CONTEXT: The 2025 American Thyroid Association (ATA) guidelines maintained the low- and high-risk categories and subdivided the intermediate-risk category of differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) into low-intermediate and intermediate-high tiers. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether observed rates of structural disease match the risks the 2025 and 2015 ATA classifications assign, and to compare the two systems. PATIENTS AND METHODS: All 258 consecutive adults with DTC diagnosed in 2017 were classified under both systems using initial postoperative data. The main outcome was structural disease at any assessment, compared against the guideline-assigned ranges. RESULTS: Sixty-three patients (24.4%) were reclassified, including 52 of 121 (43.0%) low-risk patients upstaged. Thirty-two (12.4%) developed structural disease. Observed 2025 rates were 0.0% (95% CI, 0.0-5.3), 1.5% (0.3-8.0), 15.5% (9.3-24.7), and 47.4% (32.5-62.7) for low, low-intermediate, intermediate-high, and high risk. The low-intermediate interval fell entirely below its assigned 10% to 15% range (P = .013 vs the 10% lower bound); the other categories of both systems were consistent with theirs. 42974596.abstract: Many AI models for disease prediction remain difficult to integrate into clinical practice because model complexity can limit transparent interpretation. This study develops a domain-informed, low-dimensional machine-learning framework for diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening using routinely collected electronic health record and laboratory data. Medical-domain information was extracted from PubMed using a Term Frequency-Relative Citation Ratio (TF-RCR) procedure, and the selected feature set was constrained to remain cognitively manageable. The final model uses eight variables - age, glucose, nephropathy, neuropathy, HbA1c, hemoglobin, albumin, and creatinine - and its predictions are examined using post-hoc SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) feature attribution. The data contained a 97,786-patient cohort, including 16,865 DR cases (17.25%). After a 64%/16%/20% training/validation/test split, SMOTE was applied only to the training subset, while validation and test sets retained the observed prevalence. On the untouched test set (n = 19,558), the eight-feature XGBoost model achieved 95.35% accuracy, 91.17% sensitivity, 96.22% specificity, an F1-score of 87.12%, AUROC of 97.24%, an

42972859.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between various hospital characteristics and Medicaid facility prices for several routine procedures. STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We conducted a cross-sectional study of facility claims data from Elevance Health-affiliated Medicaid plans from 22 states plus D.C. We estimated Poisson regression models where the outcome was facility allowed cost ("price") for procedures of interest, and the exposures were hospital characteristics, including children's hospital, critical access hospital (CAH), rurality, system affiliation, teaching designation, for-profit, religious affiliation, government ownership, and hospital size. We report incidence rate ratios (IRRs) from the regression estimates. DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: We analyzed 2021-2023 facility claims for 11 routine procedures in the outpatient or emergency department (ED) settings, including tympanostomy, colonoscopy, and ED evaluation and management (E/M) Levels 2-5. The claims were joined with data from the American Hospital Directory to identify hospital characteristics. The study included 2,250,325 children and 2,341,063 adults who received at least one of the procedures of interest. PRI

42967029.abstract: After cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation, acute gastric hypomotility progressed to phytobezoar formation. The admission CT had already shown a mottled intragastric mass with entrapped gas, initially interpreted as retained food; when post-ablation symptoms persist, clinicians should re-examine the original imaging before escalating therapy.

42965871.abstract: Mental distress is associated increased healthcare utilisation, but little is known about whether the relationship between mental distress and use of health care services differs between Sami and non-Sami populations in Norway. The aim of this study was to investigate whether level of mental distress was associated with a different pattern of use of primary and specialised healthcare services among Sami and non-Sami populations. Data from the SAMINOR 2 Questionnaire Survey were linked to data from the Norwegian Control and Payout of Health Refunds Database and Statistics Norway. Level of mental distress based on the 10 items Hopkins Symptom Checklist was the primary exposure variable. Participants were categorised as Sami or non-Sami and stratified by sex. Primary and specialist healthcare utilisation, and the interaction between mental distress and ethnicity, were assessed by estimating incidence rates and incidence rate ratios from Negative binomial generalised linear models with a log link. The primary model was adjusted for age, years of education, and chronic conditions. Mental distress was associated with increased utilisation of both primary and specialist healthcare service

42964649.abstract: Food fraud is an enormous challenge in the world with impact on consumer health, stability of the market, and trust. This review focuses on the key types of food fraud, such as adulteration, substitution, mislabelling and counterfeiting, as well as their ramifications with respect to food safety and regulation. For food authentication, traditional analytical methods such as chromatography, spectroscopy, and DNA-based assays are reliable but can be complicated, require a large amount of analysis, and require centralized laboratory facilities. Microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (PADs) have thus become attractive platforms for rapid and decentralized food-fraud screening. Their application to milk and dairy products, honey, edible oil, meat, drinks, seafood and functional foods is discussed. They are discussed particularly with regard to their potential for miniaturized analysis, fast detection and integration into portable readout systems. Issues that still have to be addressed are sensitivity, cross-reactivity, matrix effects, standardization, and validation in various food matrices. The need for transparency and accountability in food supply chains may be further fostered

42960248.abstract: Clear cell carcinoma arising from ovarian endometrioma is well documented; however, its origin from uterine adenomyosis is exceptionally rare. A 60-year-old postmenopausal woman with long-standing adenomyosis and no gynecologic follow-up for approximately 10 years presented with a 7 cm pelvic mass detected on routine health screening. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an intramural mass with mixed cystic and solid components, restricted diffusion, and contrast enhancement. Despite the absence of uterine bleeding and negative cervical and endometrial cytology, malignancy was suspected. Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy was performed. Histopathology confirmed clear cell carcinoma arising in adenomyosis, with transition foci from benign adenomyosis to carcinoma. This case highlights that clear cell carcinoma arising in adenomyosis should be considered when a long-standing cystic uterine lesion enlarges and develops suspicious imaging features, even in the absence of uterine bleeding or cytological abnormalities.

42959522.abstract: Peroxisomes couple hydrogen peroxide metabolism to lipid homeostasis, making their functions relevant to neurological disease and to the design of intracellular catalytic biomaterials. However, the strength of disease-specific evidence and the functions reproduced by current materials vary substantially. This narrative review distinguishes modified biological peroxisomes from artificial and biomimetic platforms and evaluates how patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models could support their development. We examine membrane chemistry, substrate permeability, enzyme retention, catalytic activity, cell targeting, blood-brain barrier transport, three-dimensional tissue penetration, and intracellular fate. We separate the established causal role of peroxisomal defects in primary peroxisomal disorders from associative or unresolved findings in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Kleefstra syndrome is discussed as a hypothesis-generating neurodevelopmental model, without assuming a primary peroxisomal defect. 42959500.abstract: Urinary organic acid (UOA) testing has established diagnostic applications in inherited metabolic disorders, but its relevance to preventive health assessment and healthy-aging research requires critical evaluation. This state-of-the-art review examines adult human evidence while distinguishing clinical organic acid testing, commercial panels, and targeted or untargeted urinary metabolomics. Eight complementary PubMed searches, supplemented by targeted reference-list checking, yielded 3054 unique records for title and abstract screening. Data from 38 human-study reports, including population characteristics, analytical methods, metabolites, outcomes, confounder adjustment, evaluation procedures, and study limitations, were extracted and synthesized narratively. Analytical and normalization strategies, interpretative limitations, and multi-omics approaches were critically appraised, distinguishing biological associations and exploratory prediction from validated clinical utility. Across the reviewed studies, urinary metabolite profiles were associated with adiposity, metabolic syndrome, renal outcomes, microbial features, and aging-related phenotypes. 42959448.abstract: Among different types of arthritis, osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remain the most common and primary cause of pain and disability worldwide, characterized by progressive joint degeneration and persistent inflammation. Although there have been developments in pharmacology, the available treatment program slows disease progression and provides only symptomatic relief. However, their ability to repair and restore damaged tissue is limited. This highlights the importance of regenerative therapy in actively modulating the immune system while stimulating tissue regeneration. We conducted a narrative review of PubMed, Scopus, Web of science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ChiCTR, focusing on preclinical and clinical studies of umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UC-MSCs) therapy in OA and RA. Recently, UC-MSC have been emerging as a promising therapeutic approach due to their immunomodulatory and regenerative properties. Because they are harvested noninvasively, these cells have greater proliferative capacity and lower immunogenicity than MSCs derived from bone marrow or adipose tissue. UC-MSCs do not replace damaged cells; instead, they signal other cells to produ

42936460.abstract: BACKGROUND: The global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis necessitates innovative therapeutic approaches beyond traditional antibiotics. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP), an ionized gas containing reactive species, has emerged as a potent physical antimicrobial technology with broad-spectrum activity. This systematic review critically evaluates current evidence on CAP's antimicrobial mechanisms, efficacy against diverse pathogens, and clinical translation potential. METHODS: We conducted a systematic literature search following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases (January 2018-December 2025). Included studies investigated CAP's antimicrobial properties in vitro, in vivo, or clinically. RESULTS: Analysis of 64 included studies revealed that CAP's antimicrobial effects primarily stem from reactive oxygen and nitrogen species generation, causing oxidative damage to microbial membranes, proteins, and DNA. CAP demonstrates significant efficacy against multi-drug-resistant bacteria, viruses, fungi, and biofilms. Clinical studies show particular promise in chronic wound management, with randomize

42936331.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The accuracy of estimating glomerular filtration rate (GFR) using endogenous biomarkers has been widely studied, and many GFR estimating equations have been proposed. In this study, we compared the performance of these equations in a Finnish population and evaluated their accuracy in different age groups and categories based on measured GFR (mGFR). METHODS: Our study included patients under the age of 20 years whose GFR was measured between September 2014 and April 2025. Patient information was collected retrospectively from the Helsinki University Hospital electronic data lake. GFR was estimated with multiple equations, using either a single analyte or a combination of analytes, and was compared with mGFR in terms of bias, precision, and accuracy. RESULTS: Our cohort consisted of 516 patients aged from 0.8 to 19.9 years with a history of solid organ transplantation, malignancy, or suspected kidney impairment. In general, creatinine-cystatin C-based combination equations exhibited better performance than single-analyte equations. 42935887.abstract: PURPOSE: Recent studies suggest distinct patterns of DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) expression across different stages of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). However, whether these variations can be modulated by conventional therapeutic approaches remains unexplored. This study investigates DNMT expression dynamics in two patients with exudative neovascular AMD (nAMD) during the initial months of anti-VEGF treatment. OBSERVATIONS: Case 1, a female in her 90s was seen for sudden loss of vision secondary to macular hemorrhage. During type 1 macular neovascularization (t1MNV) anti-VEGF treatment, DNMT analysis revealed sustained upregulation of DNMT1 (+116%) and DNMT3b (+179%) while exudative MNV remained presisted.Case 2, a female in her 70s and asymptomatic subretinal fluid secondary to t1MNV showed a distinct DNMT expression pattern, with a more modest increase in DNMT1 (+28.9%) and DNMT3b (+17.6%) when exudation was resolved. CONCLUSIONS: We hereby report varying DNMTs expression in nAMD patients with different disease manifestations giving new insights into the dynamic nature of epigenetic modifications in response to anti-VEGF treatment.

42935584.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the finding of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) in a patient with posterior ischemic optic neuropathy (PION) leading to the diagnosis of occult giant cell arteritis (GCA). CASE REPORT: A 67-year-old man presented with sudden monocular vision loss. Ophthalmic examination revealed profound vision loss with an ipsilateral relative afferent pupillary defect, a cotton wool spot and PAMM on optical coherence tomography (OCT), while the optic disc appeared normal. Fluorescein and indocyanine green angiography revealed a perfusion deficit in the nasal choroid. There were no systemic symptoms and acute phase reactants were normal. Temporal artery biopsy was negative, while temporal artery ultrasound revealed definite signs of GCA. Accordingly, the final diagnosis of arteritic PION was made. At 9-month follow-up the optic disc was atrophic, and retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) had developed at the previous locations of PAMM. CONCLUSION: PAMM on macular OCT may occasionally be the only indication of GCA in patients with sudden vision loss. 42928446.abstract: At membrane contact sites (MCSs) between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and endolysosomal compartments, the Protrudin-PDZD8 complex promotes the maturation of endosomes into lysosomes, a process accompanied by acidification. Endosomal maturation is closely associated with both lysosomal acidification and calcium signaling; however, the molecular mechanisms linking the Protrudin-PDZD8 complex to these processes remain unclear. Here, we identified TMEM55B, a lysosome-localized protein, as a binding partner of the Protrudin-PDZD8 complex. TMEM55B has been reported to interact with the v-ATPase complex, suggesting a role in lysosomal function. Suppression of TMEM55B expression reduced the fluorescence of a lysosomal acidification probe, suggesting impaired lysosomal acidification. In addition, TMEM55B depletion attenuated lysosomal Ca2+ release and reuptake and reduced ATP-induced Ca2+ responses in the ER. These findings suggest impaired calcium-induced calcium release (CICR) at ER-lysosome MCSs. By contrast, mitochondrial Ca2+ dynamics were unaffected. Together, these results identify TMEM55B as a factor involved in maintaining lysosomal homeostasis and regulating calcium dynamics. Ou

42927200.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders are a major cause of pain, disability, and loss of function. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been widely investigated for musculoskeletal repair, and interest has increasingly extended to extracellular vesicle (EV) preparations obtained from platelet-related starting materials. These include EV-enriched preparations collected from isolated platelets or defined platelet concentrates (P-EVs), from PRP (PRP-EVs), and from platelet lysate (PL-EVs). They do not represent the same biological product. Their cellular contributors, co-isolated soluble components, and molecular composition can differ substantially, and the name of the starting material does not prove the origin of every vesicle in the preparation. Preclinical studies nevertheless suggest that these EV preparations can influence inflammatory responses, cartilage metabolism, tendon-cell behavior, and the local repair environment. The strength of this evidence varies with the source material, separation and characterization methods, experimental model, and delivery strategy. This review examines the therapeutic evidence for platelet-related EV preparations in musculoskeletal disorders, while keeping P-E

42926817.abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries remain difficult to treat because axonal regeneration is slow, incomplete, and highly dependent on timely biochemical, structural, and electrical cues. Self-powered electroceuticals offer an emerging route to deliver localized electrical stimulation with reduced dependence on bulky batteries and percutaneous leads. This review summarizes recent advances in self-powered bioelectronic systems for nerve repair, with emphasis on three representative platforms: self-electrified galvanic devices, triboelectric nanogenerators, and piezoelectric nanogenerators. From a materials and interfacial engineering perspective, we discuss how redox reactions, contact electrification, and piezoelectric polarization convert physiological or externally applied energy into therapeutic electrical outputs. Key design factors, including biodegradable metals, electroactive polymers, piezoelectric composites, conductive interfaces, encapsulation strategies, and nerve-guidance architectures, are critically examined in relation to output stability, degradation behavior, tissue compatibility, and regenerative efficacy. We further highlight preclinical evidence that self-powered electri

42920360.abstract: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis is a process by which eukaryotic cells internalise a wide range of molecules such as signalling factors, nutrients and membrane proteins, via the formation of a plasma-membrane-derived vesicle. This complex mechanism involves a coordinated assembly of the scaffold protein clathrin and more than 50 other endocytic proteins at endocytic sites. Clathrin polymerises into sturdy supramolecular lattices, yet its assembly is highly dynamic and controlled by the DnaJ/Hsc70 uncoating machinery. Although clathrin turnover at endocytic sites was proposed early on to allow membrane deformation to occur, more recent studies have started hinting at possible regulatory functions. In this review, we summarise and discuss the key findings that have advanced our understanding of the role played by clathrin dynamics, hoping to shed light on the complex regulation of the endocytic process.

42913294.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-engineered cells can converge on the same surface antigens in urothelial carcinoma (UC) yet depend on distinct biological steps. This creates a central uncertainty after ADC progression: whether failure reflects loss of membrane antigen or a downstream resistance mechanism that a CAR might bypass. We synthesize paired human tissue, molecular-imaging, ADC-resistance and UC-specific CAR-cell studies to examine whether an antigen targeted by a failed ADC remains suitable for cellular therapy. NECTIN4 after enfortumab vedotin (EV) provides the most direct evidence. Membranous expression often decreases between primary and metastatic UC, and serial observations document lesion-specific loss. However, selected post-EV biopsies and resistant models retain NECTIN4; in those models, NECTIN4 CAR T cells remain active. Transporter and payload-resistance studies further support target-independent failure. Evidence for HER2 and TROP2 is less direct but suggests that alternative antigens may remain available when NECTIN4 declines. We therefore propose a resistance-state framework: same-target CAR development requires recent evid

42909857.abstract: In biomedical engineering, hydrogel bioelectronics brings together the interface between flexible electronic devices and biological systems, opening up a new way for chronic neural regulation. Here we focus on the recent progress in this field, from material design to system integration. The design of high-performance conductive hydrogels is an entry point. The multi-level structure engineering strategy, such as the introduction of carbon nanotubes or conductive polymers, can raise the conductivity and mechanical toughness together. When biomimetic adhesion molecules such as polydopamine or tannic acid are added, the hydrogel has the ability of wet tissue adhesion, and anti swelling and active anti-inflammatory functions are also embedded in the material system. As a result, the resulting neural interfaces are not only more durable in practical applications but also ensure excellent biocompatibility. Turning to applications. How does this kind of material promote the development of chronic neuromodulation technology? 42900683.abstract: Background: Drama-based techniques have been increasingly implemented with trauma-exposed populations. However, the evidence base remains conceptually and methodologically heterogeneous, with substantial variation in how trauma is defined, how interventions are described, and which trauma-related outcomes are assessed.Objective: This review aimed to synthesise empirical studies examining drama-based interventions for individuals exposed to trauma. The review describes the characteristics of drama-based interventions, the types of trauma addressed, the pattern and range of trauma-related psychological outcomes assessed, and the methodological quality and certainty of the available evidence.Methods: A search was conducted across Scopus, PsycINFO, MEDLINE, and Web of Science Core Collection databases on 29 October 2025. Studies published in English within the past 20 years were eligible if they examined a drama-based intervention in a trauma-exposed population and reported trauma-related psychological outcomes. 42896592.abstract: An ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS) method was applied to characterize Pingchuanning (PCN) decoction and its absorbed serum constituents in asthmatic rats. A total of 107 compounds were identified in PCN, of which 36 prototypes were detected in rat serum. Network pharmacology and molecular docking of these absorbed compounds predicted ADORA2A as the core therapeutic target, with 5-O-methylvisammioside, nobiletin, sec-O-glucosylhamaudol, and 9-oxo-ODE showing binding affinity. In an ovalbumin-induced asthmatic rat model, PCN alleviated airway hyperresponsiveness and lung inflammation. Mechanistically, PCN upregulated ADORA2A, elevated cAMP and PKA phosphorylation, and suppressed NLRP3 expression. This UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS-based serum pharmacochemistry method effectively identified the bioactive components of PCN, and the integrated strategy demonstrates that PCN exerts anti-asthmatic effects through the ADORA2A/cAMP/PKA/NLRP3 axis.

42881531.abstract: Efficient delivery of plasmid DNA (pDNA) into the nucleus remains a major bottleneck in nonviral gene therapy, particularly in post-mitotic and slowly dividing cells where the nuclear envelope constitutes a permanent barrier to passive entry. This review considers the two main strategies for active nuclear targeting: nuclear localisation signal (NLS) peptides, which recruit importin-α/β receptors directly to DNA cargo, and DNA nuclear targeting sequences (DTS), which exploit NLS-bearing transcription factors to mediate piggyback nuclear import. Rather than re-cataloguing nuclear import biology, we focus on the conditions under which each strategy succeeds or fails, incorporating advances in nuclear pore complex architecture and permeability, karyopherin-FG-nucleoporin electrostatics, and cytoplasmic constraints such as barrier-to-autointegration factor (BAF)-mediated clustering of exogenous DNA. NLS classes are compared with universal (SV40 enhancer), inducible (NF-κB) and tissue-specific (SMGA, SP-C, T1α) DTS elements, and four chemical coupling strategies are evaluated across peptide-, polymer- and lipid-based nanoassemblies. To address the near-absence of NLS/DTS mechanisms in c

42876306.abstract: Chemical modifications of RNA bases and adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing are regulatory layers essentially unexplored in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), whose oxidative dysfunction underlies age-related macular degeneration. We mapped both layers in ARPE-19 cells exposed to tert-butyl hydroperoxide under two non-pharmacological interventions, Quantum Molecular Resonance (QMR) electrotherapy and a patient blood-derived secretome, across 56 libraries spanning four arms, three time points and matched stressed and stress-free conditions (GEO: GSE328981). Base modifications were called with HARMLNC and A-to-I editing screened with a transition-signal caller, then re-analysed with REDItools3, JACUSA2 and LoDEI. The high-confidence set comprised 241 calls at 15 sites, all of classes canonical to tRNA and rRNA. The most prevalent was an adenosine modification at chrM:2617 in mitochondrial 16S rRNA (MT-RNR2), detected in 51 of 56 libraries and in every arm. Two positions 1 bp apart lie in an EZR/SYTL3 overlap region, whereas a third chromosome 6 site maps to HLA-C, 127.5 Mb away. 42873904.abstract: BACKGROUND: γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) accumulates under stress, but its association with calcium (Ca2+), reactive oxygen species (ROS), nitric oxide (NO), and thiol responses during cadmium (Cd) exposure remains unclear in medicinal shrubs. METHODS: Rooted Salvadora persica L. cuttings were grown in sand-soil substrate. Screening selected 50mg Cd kg-1 substrate and 0.5  mM root-applied GABA. Eleven treatments had five independent pots each. Ca2+-sensitive Fluo-3 AM and NO-associated DAF-FM DA fluorescence and H₂O₂ were assessed in separate, destructively sampled plants at five post-application times. The 0-min value was a post-application reference; probe fluorescence was not calibrated to analyte concentration. Pot means were independent units, with time treated as a between-pot factor. A core Cd × GABA × time model and a separate categorical endpoint model were specified. The exact p-values, adjusted q-values, and model diagnostics could not be verified without pot-level records. Correlation and principal component analyses were exploratory; no path model was fitted. 42831209.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast cancer (BC) is the leading cancer among women worldwide until 2050. Indonesia has developed a 10-year national cancer plan to increase screening uptake. Having a BRCA1/2 gene mutation, the most common cause of hereditary BC, was found to increase uptake. Unfortunately, an expensive, non-government-funded test is necessary to check mutation status. Therefore, this study is the first in Indonesia to explore willingness to pay (WTP) for the test, along with knowledge, perceptions, acceptance, and the significance of having a mutation on intention to screen. METHODS: An exploratory, cross-sectional, online, 7-section survey using non-probability sampling in October-November 2025 among females aged ≥25 residing in Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta. Unadjusted Spearman's rank, unadjusted Kruskal-Wallis, Cochran's Q, and McNemar's tests were used to determine relationships. RESULTS: Of 400 females, most had low knowledge levels, perceived high benefits and moderate barriers, and were willing to undergo testing and pay for it. 42828513.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fatty liver disease is frequently identified during routine health examinations, but practical strategies for risk stratification in adults with thyroid dysfunction remain limited. This study evaluated metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) prevalence across thyroid function categories and developed health examination-based risk stratification models. METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 46,311 adults who underwent routine health examinations from November 2019 to February 2025. Participants were classified as euthyroid, hypothyroid, or hyperthyroid. MAFLD was defined as ultrasound-confirmed hepatic steatosis plus overweight/obesity, diabetes, or metabolic dysregulation. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses assessed thyroid-related associations. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression were used to develop models for adults with hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism. 42824489.abstract: Bone organoids are emerging as three-dimensional models of skeletal development, disease and regeneration. The term bone organoid is applied inconsistently to osteogenic spheroids, scaffold-dominated constructs and self-organizing skeletal tissues. This review establishes an operational five-class framework that distinguishes osteogenic spheroids, bone-like microtissues, engineered skeletal constructs, bone organoids and high-fidelity bone organoids. Core organoid criteria are separated from advanced, application-dependent features, and a structured evidence map applies the terminology to representative original studies. We summarize the coordinated osteogenic, chondrogenic, vascular, neural and immune programs that govern bone formation and examine how cell source, induction sequence, matrix composition, mass transport and mechanical stimulation affect maturation. Inkjet, extrusion, laser-assisted and photocuring-based bioprinting are compared using common technical and biological criteria, including resolution, viscosity, cell density, injury mechanisms, mineral compatibility, perfusable channels, scalability and direct bone-organoid evidence. 42820785.abstract: Nose-to-brain (N2B) delivery is a promising noninvasive strategy to circumvent the blood‒brain barrier (BBB). However, the clinical translation of N2B platforms remains hindered by a conceptual oversimplification that equates crude central nervous system (CNS) exposure with effective therapeutic delivery. This review reconceptualizes the N2B pathway as a stage-resolved sequential transport cascade extending from nasal entry to meaningful parenchymal and cellular access. We identify a critical imbalance in current formulation strategies, which have advanced two extreme poles, namely initial mucosal retention and epithelial permeation at one end and final target-cell engagement at the other, while leaving the intermediate post-epithelial gateways, including cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and perivascular space (PVS)-mediated redistribution and deep intraparenchymal diffusion, as structural and interpretive blind spots. To bridge this gap, we propose an integrated engineering paradigm with three core design principles.
