42816924.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To systematically review the evidence for orthotic interventions on pain, balance, and plantar pressure distribution in individuals with flexible flatfoot. METHODS: Randomized and nonrandomized controlled trials of orthotic interventions for flexible flatfoot were included. Primary outcomes were pain, balance, and plantar pressure. MEDLINE via PubMed, EMBASE via Elsevier, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to October 16, 2025. All effect sizes were independently recomputed, and pooling required two or more compatible datasets. RESULTS: Eight studies with 382 participants were included: six randomized controlled trials, one nonrandomized controlled trial, and one within-subject repeated-measures study. No domain met the pooling condition, so all previously reported summary estimates and heterogeneity statistics are withdrawn. Pain against a comparator without arch support rested on Yurt et al. (n = 67): g = -1.02 [95% CI: -1.54, -0.49] on the trial's designated primary outcome, a 100 mm visual analog scale, but g = -0.28 on its Foot Function Index total. In Elsayed et al. (n = 40) both arms wore the same orthosis, so g = -0.97 [-1.62, -0.33] estimates a

42787934.abstract: PURPOSE: To report a novel observation of peripheral inner retinal dimples (IRDs) in a patient with X-linked retinoschisis (XLRS). METHODS: A 30-year-old male with molecularly confirmed XLRS presented for his regular follow up with a new complaint of photopsia for the past month preceding examination. He underwent complete ophthalmological examination and multimodal imaging with special emphasis on peripheral retinal changes. Ultrawide-field color fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), fluorescein angiography optical coherence tomography angiography (UWF-OCTA) were done. RESULTS: His best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/40 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye with unremarkable anterior segment examination. Fundus examination demonstrated foveoschisis associated with peripheral retinal changes most notable in the inferiorotemporal quadrant manifesting as with horizontal, band-like vitreous membrane. UWF multimodal imaging confirmed presence of inner retinal dimples which corresponded to hyporeflective dark spots observed on enface OCT and UWF OCTA. CONCLUSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of IRDs in the inferotemporal quadrants of th

42787855.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive biliary malignancy with increasing incidence and poor prognosis. Although traditionally considered a disease of older adults, early-onset CCA (EOCCA; age <50 years) may represent a clinically distinct subgroup. Data evaluating diagnostic and treatment trajectories in EOCCA remain limited. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Using the Komodo Healthcare Map claims database (2017-2024), patients with CCA were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, codes and categorized as having EOCCA or average-onset CCA. Outcomes included time from first diagnosed symptom to CCA diagnosis, diagnostic delay (≥30 days), time to first intervention, and type of first intervention. Multivariable logistic, log-gamma, and competing-risk regression models evaluated associations between demographic and insurance factors and care delivery outcomes. RESULTS: Among 116 106 patients with CCA, 5146 (4.4%) had EOCCA. Of 43 137 patients with symptoms documented in their claims data, EOCCA was independently associated with longer time to diagnosis [expβ 1.13, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.07-1.20, P < 0.001] and higher odds of diagnostic del

42774990.abstract: Alport syndrome is a hereditary glomerular basement membrane disorder caused by pathogenic variants in COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5. Autosomal dominant forms are increasingly recognized but remain underdiagnosed due to their mild and heterogeneous presentation. We report the case of a 38-year-old woman referred for persistent proteinuria and microscopic hematuria with preserved renal function. Extensive immunological and infectious work-up was negative. Kidney biopsy revealed minimal abnormalities on light microscopy and negative immunofluorescence. Electron microscopy demonstrated irregular thinning of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), with focal thickening, lamellation, and segmental splitting of the lamina densa, without immune-type deposits. These findings suggested a collagen IV-related nephropathy. Whole-exome sequencing identified a previously undescribed heterozygous missense variant in COL4A4 (c.4556C > G; p.Thr1519Arg). According to ACMG/AMP criteria, the variant is currently classified as a Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS), fulfilling PM1, PM2, and PP3 evidence criteria. Nevertheless, the combination of the patient's phenotype, characteristic ultrastructural fi

42761636.abstract: Secondary esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is an uncommon but recognized late malignancy after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, particularly in patients with chronic graft-versus-host disease. We report a 33-year-old man with T-cell lymphoma treated approximately 8 years earlier with chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, complicated by chronic cutaneous and ocular graft-versus-host disease. He developed 6 months of progressive dysphagia and weight loss; upper endoscopy with biopsy confirmed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, and he completed 6 cycles of preoperative chemotherapy. When severe oral intolerance prompted admission, barium swallow demonstrated an irregular short-segment mid-thoracic esophageal stricture at the carina with mild proximal dilatation and approximately 2.5 cm of linear contrast extravasation toward the left bronchial tree, raising suspicion for a bronchoesophageal fistula. Chest computed tomography showed an approximately 70-mm elongated mid-esophageal mass with proximal fluid-filled dilatation. Contemporaneous neck and abdominopelvic computed tomography showed no definite distant metastasis

42761632.abstract: Amyand's hernia is a rare clinical entity defined by the presence of the vermiform appendix within an inguinal hernia sac, with acute appendicitis occurring in this setting being exceptionally uncommon. We report the case of a 57-year-old male who presented with pain in a known right inguinal hernia. Clinical evaluation demonstrated an incarcerated right inguinal hernia, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed an inflamed appendix herniating into the right inguinal canal, consistent with acute appendicitis within an Amyand's hernia. The patient underwent urgent laparoscopic exploration, which confirmed an acutely inflamed, gangrenous appendix partially contained within the hernia sac. A laparoscopic appendectomy was successfully performed, and the appendix was reduced from the hernia sac. Given the gangrenous nature of the appendix and concerns regarding microperforation and potential infection, inguinal hernia repair was deferred. The patient recovered without immediate complications. This case highlights the diagnostic value of preoperative imaging, the feasibility of a minimally invasive approach, and the importance of individualized surgical decision-making for Amyand'

42791617.abstract: BACKGROUND: Celiac disease (CeD) is an autoimmune enteropathy in which diagnosis and disease monitoring rely on serology and small-intestinal histology. However, conventional histological assessment is semi-quantitative, subject to interobserver variability, and relatively insensitive to subtle mucosal changes, particularly in treated patients or during early disease. Recent advances in transcriptomic technologies have enabled detailed characterization of intestinal mucosal gene expression, revealing disease-specific molecular signatures. This review aims to synthesize current evidence on molecular histomorphometry and to evaluate the emerging role of transcriptomic profiling in improving diagnosis, disease monitoring, and therapeutic trial endpoints in CeD. In addition, we propose practical guidelines and a methodological pipeline for implementing transcriptomic analyses in this context. DISCUSSION: Transcriptomic analyses consistently identify characteristic epithelial and immune activation signatures in active CeD, including interferon-driven pathways, epithelial stress responses, and loss of mature enterocyte differentiation. Importantly, persistent molecular abnormalities are

42715795.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Precise and scalable instance segmentation of cell nuclei is a fundamental prerequisite for computational pathology, yet gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) pose significant computational challenges. While patch-based processing is standard during training, existing methods are often limited to small tile sizes during inference due to architectural bottlenecks or reliance on computationally expensive post-processing steps for instance separation. We introduce a faster, scalable, and end-to-end framework capable of processing large-scale image tiles while accurately modeling biologically realistic overlapping nuclei. METHODS: We propose LSP-DETR (Local Star Polygon DEtection TRansformer). The model represents nuclei as star-convex polygons and employs a lightweight transformer with linear complexity, enabling the processing of high-resolution images in a single forward pass. A novel radial distance loss accommodates annotation uncertainty, allowing the segmentation of overlapping nuclei to emerge naturally without explicit overlap labels. RESULTS: LSP-DETR achieves state-of-the-art efficiency, with an inference time of 0.45 s/mm2 representing a 3.2× speedup

42548065.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Accurate assessment of mitotic activity is an important component of melanoma prognostication but remains challenging due to interobserver variability and difficulties in identifying representative mitotic hotspots. We developed and evaluated a deep learning-based mitosis detection algorithm for whole-slide images (WSIs) of melanoma and investigated its utility for hotspot identification and spatial analysis of mitotic distribution. METHODS: The model was trained on manually annotated histopathology images and applied to a cohort of 114 melanoma cases comprising 378 WSIs. Performance was assessed against expert annotation using sensitivity, precision, and F1-score. Algorithm-identified hotspots were reviewed by a pathologist and compared with mitotic counts reported in routine clinical practice. Spatial organization of mitotic figures was evaluated using nearest-neighbour distance analyses. RESULTS: The algorithm achieved a sensitivity of 88%, precision of 75%, and an F1 score of 0.81, demonstrating strong agreement with expert assessment. Across the cohort, 30,547 mitotic figures were detected, enabling comprehensive whole-slide analysis of proliferative activity. AI

42530379.abstract: BACKGROUND: Distinguishing melanoma cells from nevus cells remains a diagnostic challenge, particularly in cases where melanoma exhibits nevoid morphology or nevus cells display atypical or epithelioid features. Accurate identification is essential for proper measurement of Breslow depth in melanomas arising in association with nevi and for margin assessment, both of which are critical for patient prognosis. The dual multiplex immunohistochemical stain utilizing Melan-A (red chromogen) and Ki67 (brown chromogen) is a valuable tool for assessing the proliferative index of melanocytic populations, with melanoma cells typically showing a higher Ki67 index than nevus cells. METHODS: We identified 10 cases with invasive melanoma and associated nevus present on the same scanned histologic section for which the signing pathologist had ordered this dual multiplex immunohistochemical study. We annotated areas of melanoma versus nevus, then quantified the staining intensities. RESULTS: Melanoma cells often demonstrate more intense Melan-A red chromogen labeling than adjacent nevus cells (p = 0.008; Wilcoxon signed rank test). CONCLUSION: This differential labeling provides a helpful visual d

41992828.abstract: BACKGROUND: To develop and validate an integrated radiopathomics nomogram combining multiphase CT images, H&E-stained slides, and clinicopathological variables for predicting microvascular patterns (MVPs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: We retrospectively included consecutive surgically resected NSCLC patients from two centers (n = 258). Patients from center 1 were randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts, while patients from center 2 formed external validation cohort. CD34-immunohistochemistry was used as the reference standard for MVPs to classify patients into non-angiogenic alveolar (NAA) and non-NAA groups. Radiomics and pathomics features were extracted to construct single-phase radiomics, combined radiomics, and pathomics models. Rad-score and Path-score were derived from combined radiomics and pathomics models, respectively. Rad-score, Path-score, and clinicopathological independent predictors were integrated to develop a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA), and DeLong test. RESULTS: On multivariable analysis, histological grade was an independent predi

41876962.abstract: Tubulointerstitial inflammation (TII) serves as a critical nexus connecting glomerular injury, interstitial fibrosis, and kidney function decline, and is commonly observed across various glomerular diseases. Pathogenic drivers and crosstalk along the glomerulus-tubule-interstitium axis promote a persistent interstitial inflammatory microenvironment, wherein chemokines, cytokines, and adhesion molecules activate specific pathways to recruit immune cells. Despite increasing attention, the independent prognostic significance of TII remains inconsistent across different diseases and populations. Moreover, glomerulus-centric therapies have failed to halt disease progression in a substantial subset of patients, highlighting the limitations of strategies focused solely on the glomerulus. Methodological variations - such as denominator definitions (total cortex vs. non-fibrotic cortex), scoring systems (percentage-based vs. count/semi-quantitative methods), and inconsistent covariate adjustment - largely account for these discrepancies. This review systematically synthesizes current evidence on the pathogenic mechanisms, prognostic relevance, and translational limitations of TII in glomeru

42999554.abstract: This article provides an overview of digital pathology and its evolving role in modern diagnostic practice. We begin by comparing conventional microscopy with digital pathology and outlining the major components of the digital pathology workflow. We then explore whole-slide imaging, its imaging modalities, scanner technologies, image storage, and image management systems. We then examine the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital pathology, discussing current AI applications and the spectrum of computational approaches, from conventional feature-engineering methods to deep learning and multimodal models. Finally, we review the clinical applications of digital pathology, summarize its implementation across US medical centers, and discuss the technical, regulatory, and operational challenges that must be addressed for broader clinical adoption.

42999375.abstract: Evidence on the real-world impact of artificial intelligence (AI) decision support on diagnostic efficiency and workflow outcomes in primary breast cancer pathology remains limited. This retrospective, single-site, paired reader, two-arm study evaluated the impact of AI-assisted digital pathology (DP + AI) versus standard DP on workflow efficiency and diagnostic performance in digitized consecutive breast biopsy cases. Primary endpoints were pathologist review time, lab turnaround time (TAT), and usability (survey-based). Secondary endpoints included diagnostic performance of pathologists across both arms and standalone AI against adjudicated reference standard. Analyses included descriptive statistics, paired t-test, and diagnostic performance metrics with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The study included 194 digitized breast biopsies. The mean pathologist overall review time was reduced by 43.5% in DP + AI (40.18 [95% CI: 36.20-44.16] s) versus DP (71.12 [95% CI: 64.39-77.84] s) (p < 0.0001). Diagnostic agreement was 97.42% with DP and 99.48% with DP + AI, with 100% sensitivity observed in the DP + AI workflow. The standalone AI showed high diagnostic accuracy, with area under t

42998450.abstract: BACKGROUND: Perineural invasion (PNI) in tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is associated with aggressive behavior and poor outcomes, yet it can be under-recognized on H&E sections because it is often focal and interpretation varies. Manual assessment of PNI suffers from significant interobserver variability, motivating AI-based decision support. We developed and externally validated a weakly supervised WSI model to predict PNI in TSCC. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,511 digitized H&E whole-slide images from 629 patients at two centers. Patient-level partitioning yielded an internal training cohort of 305 patients and 787 WSIs, an internal validation cohort of 132 patients and 340 WSIs, and an external test cohort of 192 patients and 384 WSIs. Non-overlapping tiling generated 41,552,500 candidate patches before tissue-background exclusion, of which 7,813,555 unique tissue patches were retained for analysis. A two-stage pipeline was used: patch-level modeling and MIL-based slide aggregation. ResNet50 was selected over Inception_v3 and SimpleViT as the feature extractor. Patch-level prediction probabilities and image features were aggregated into a 101-dimensional patch li

42997577.abstract: AIMS: Muscle biopsy assessment relies on descriptive features that are difficult to compare across samples. We developed MyoPath to quantify these features and examined their usefulness in clinical biopsies and population-based autopsy material. METHODS: MyoPath combines Cellpose-SAM and conventional image analysis within QuPath to segment myofibers, fat, nuclei, and connective tissue. We analyzed 478 hematoxylin and eosin images from HuashanMuscle (79 snap-frozen biopsies) and GTEx (399 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded autopsy samples). Thirty-seven features were summarized by seven pathology indicators. A composite model trained on GTEx healthy and wasting strata was transferred to HuashanMuscle without retraining. RESULTS: Segmentation Dice coefficients ranged from 0.87 to 0.95 on annotated cryosections. Nuclear centralization index (NCI) and fiber size coefficient of variation (fiber CV) discriminated myopathy from controls in HuashanMuscle (AUC 0.85 and 0.79) and wasting from healthy donors in GTEx (0.74 and 0.74). Their GTEx associations changed little after age and sex adjustment. The composite achieved AUC 0.788 (95% CI 0.71-0.85) in GTEx and 0.873 (0.78-0.94) in HuashanMu

42995188.abstract: Three-dimensional virtual histology using synchrotron radiation micro-computed tomography enables non-destructive visualization of biological tissue microarchitecture with isotropic resolution. To support quantitative studies of human pancreatic morphology, we provide high-resolution 3D X-ray imaging datasets of 55 pancreatic tissue cores from 32 individuals. The collection comprises histologically non-diseased pancreatic tissue from organ donors and non-neoplastic regions of surgical resection specimens from patients with pancreatic cancer, including subgroups with insulin-dependent diabetes or following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue cores with a diameter of 1 mm were imaged at 650 nm isotropic voxel size, yielding a mean effective spatial resolution of 1.66 µm. The cohort includes reconstructed volumes, corresponding immunohistochemistry, clinical metadata, expert-validated annotations, and dataset-specific example 2.5D U-Net models for automated segmentation of islets of Langerhans. A representative co-registered section yielded a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.81 and intersection-over-union of 0.67. This openly accessible, FAIR-compliant r

42994624.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate quantification of inflammatory cells in Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS)-stained kidney transplant biopsies is essential for Banff classification but remains subjective and labor-intensive. To address this, the MONKEY challenge benchmarked deep learning (DL) methods for automated detection of mononuclear leukocytes and their subtypes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicenter dataset of 118 biopsies with co-registered PAS and immunohistochemically restained slides, comprising over 131,000 annotated cells, was used. The algorithms were evaluated on hold-out validation and test set using Free-response Receiver Operating Characteristic (FROC) analysis, alongside precision, recall, and F1-scores. RESULTS: Across diverse architectures, performance converged, with the top models achieving F1-scores up to 0.75 for overall detection. Lymphocyte detection performed well (F1 up to 0.78), whereas monocyte detection remained more challenging (F1 up to 0.47). To explore the potential clinical applicability of automated inflammatory cell detection, the winning model was integrated with renal tissue segmentation models, enabling compartment-specific evaluation and quantitative assessment o

42991688.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitotic activity is a recognized marker of tumor proliferation, yet its reproducible assessment across whole-slide images (WSIs) remains difficult. We developed a transfer-learning framework for lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) and evaluated whether a patch-derived tumor-area mitosis proportion (TAMP) was associated with survival and molecular tumor characteristics. METHODS: The analysis combined MIDOG 2022 with TCGA-LUSC, including 478 patients and 512 diagnostic WSIs after quality control. Tumor regions and mitotic figures were reviewed by two pathologists with interobserver agreement of Cohen's κ ≥ 0.85. A ResNet-50 model was trained on MIDOG and subsequently adapted to TCGA-LUSC using Focal Loss and stain-aware augmentation. Target-domain performance was evaluated using patient-level stratified 5-fold cross-validation and an additional WSI-level holdout analysis to address potential leakage from the initial patch-level partitioning. TAMP was calculated from patient-level out-of-fold predictions as the proportion of evaluable tumor patches classified as mitosis-positive. Associations with overall survival, immune and genomic features, transcriptomic programs, pred

42989449.abstract: Recurrence in oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) remains a prognostic challenge, which necessitates additional prognostic approaches reflecting tumor biology. Therefore, we developed an objective, observer-independent, multiparametric model incorporating features of the tumoral and stromal compartments. Digitized whole-slide images from 80 patients with TSCC were analyzed using a combination of semi-automatic and deep learning-based approaches. We extracted quantitative histomorphological features, including tumor/stroma ratio (TSR), lymphocyte/stromal cell ratio in the tumor stroma (LSCR), and the modified Polsby-Popper (MPP) score reflecting tumor disjointedness. Human trophoblast cell surface glycoprotein (Trop-2) expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry in central and invasive-front tumor regions sampled via tissue microarrays (TMA) and quantified using the H-score. A composite score (CS) was constructed by summing points from these parameters; as Trop-2 did not improve cross-validated discrimination, a final three-marker CS (TSR, LSCR, MPP) was adopted as the final model. Patients were stratified into prognostic groups and recurrence-free survival (RFS) was anal

42988783.abstract: The immune-fibrotic axis functions as a vicious feedback loop where age-related chronic, low-grade systemic inflammation (inflammaging) drives maladaptive tissue repair and fibrosis, while senescent fibrotic cells in turn amplify systemic inflammation. In the aging heart, immune dysregulation and fibroblast activation drive tissue scarring and stiffening and a higher risk of heart failure and vascular disease. To identify cardiac regions and cell types affected with age, we monitored transcriptional changes across whole hearts of 6- and 24-month-old male and female mice. Spatially resolved signatures of macrophages and fibroblasts, non-cardiomyocyte populations highly involved in inflammaging, were enriched predominantly in the valves and aorta. With age, two cell types simultaneously adopted maladaptive programs: Macrophages displayed reduced immune homeostasis together with increased chemotactic and stromal programs, while more widely distributed fibroblast-lineage cells displayed alterations in extracellular matrix organization and intercellular signals, as well as upregulation of senescence-associated Cdkn1a (encoding p21) and other activated features shared with human cardiac

42985613.abstract: An Asia-enriched survey of 239 respondents found that reported implementation of spatial biology and three-dimensional pathology varied across self-rated experience groups. Respondents identified cost, analytical complexity, limited standardization, and insufficient interdisciplinary expertise as barriers, highlighting the needs for practical workflows and computational support.

42982324.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous joint disease characterized by marked variability in etiology and clinical symptoms. We aimed to determine whether spatial organization of synovial tissue underlies clinically relevant heterogeneity in knee OA. METHODS: We developed a deep learning-based semantic segmentation framework to analyze hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images of human synovium. Spatial entropy and inter-tissue connectivity metrics were incorporated to evaluate local pathology. We further applied graph neural network-based community modeling to classify tissue structures based on their microenvironment. RESULTS: The model identified key OA-associated histological features, including synovial lining hyperplasia, immune cell infiltration, angiogenesis, and fibrotic remodeling. Quantitative analysis of tissue composition revealed that enrichment of dense fibrous tissue was associated with poorer postoperative outcomes. However, tissue proportion alone did not adequately capture baseline disease status. Inter-tissue connectivity-based analysis showed that enrichment of Lining-Micro vessel interactions was associated with lower preoperative KOOS Sympto

42981766.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study sought to construct a deep-learning pipeline using an attention mechanism and multiple-instance learning (MIL) to predict early treatment response to epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) directly from routinely available hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) of pretreatment tissue in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). METHODS: We retrospectively obtained clinicopathological data from 100 patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. The model employed ResNet-50 for feature representation and integrated a gated-attention pooling mechanism for feature aggregation at the patient level. This weakly supervised approach did not require pixel-level manual annotations and enabled direct slide-level prediction of early treatment response. RESULTS: The proposed gated-attention model attained an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.891 in 5-fold cross-validation, which was numerically higher than those of mean pooling (0.837), max pooling (0.821), ABMIL (0.869), CLAM (0.874), and TransMIL (0.863); however, the difference relative to CLAM did not reach statistical significance

42977688.abstract: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are recognized as critical components of the colorectal cancer (CRC) immune microenvironment, demonstrating significant prognostic and predictive implications. However, a clear and widely accepted definition of colorectal TILs has not yet been established, and TILs are not systematically used as biomarkers in current oncology practice. This highlights the need for standardized assessment methods and a deeper understanding of the complex role of TILs in CRC, necessitating collaborative work to achieve clinical importance. This report, on behalf of the International Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Working Group (ITWG), provides a comprehensive overview of TILs in CRC, including a TILs-assessment method. It details their multifaceted role of TILs within the tumour microenvironment, details current and emerging methods for their assessment and reviews their prognostic and predictive importance. The report also explores the relationship of TILs to other established and emerging biomarkers in CRC. Emerging trends, including AI-driven analysis for automated TIL quantification, and single-cell and spatial technologies for in-depth characterization of the tu

42976068.abstract: Stain normalization is a fundamental preprocessing technique in digital and computational pathology, and it is important for improving the consistency of clinical diagnosis by reducing color heterogeneity. However, existing stain normalization methods are often limited by content-stain entanglement and an ambiguously modeled content-stain relationship, resulting in unstable structural preservation, cross-center adaptation burden, and sensitivity to template selection. To address these limitations, we propose a Vector-Quantized Content-Stain Decoupling Network (VQ-CSDN) that decouples structure-defining content from stain appearance and learns a center-specific content-to-stain mapping, enabling structure-preserving, template-free stain transfer from unseen source centers without source-specific retraining. VQ-CSDN employs two independent encoders to extract content and stain features respectively and a generator for reconstruction. To better characterize cross-center content feature spaces and capture staining styles, we introduce vector quantization with a global content codebook shared across centers and center-specific stain codebooks. Moreover, a content-to-stain module directl

42975707.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) wit

42969399.abstract: Longitudinal studies of liver injury require models that can be maintained with simple administration, low procedure-related stress, and acceptable survival. Drinking-water thioacetamide (TAA-DW) is useful for this purpose, but it mainly produces centrilobular hepatocellular injury. Few drinking-water models are available for cholestatic liver injury. Here, we tested whether 4,4'-methylenedianiline (MDA), a known bile-duct-damaging hepatotoxicant, can be used to build a practical drinking-water model of cholestatic liver injury in mice. Male C57BL/6JJcl mice received MDA in drinking water for up to 28 days. A route- and administration-schedule-matched TAA-DW model was used as a reference. Drinking-water MDA (MDA-DW) caused sustained ALT elevation without observed mortality under the tested regimen. Compared with TAA-DW, MDA-DW produced stronger cholestatic biochemical features, including increased ALP, TBIL, and TCHO. Histology showed bile duct hyperplasia with degeneration, periportal/peribiliary fibrosis, and scattered focal hepatocellular necrosis. Whole-slide image analysis supported the distinct lesion distribution between MDA-DW and TAA-DW. Early time-resolved multimodal prof

42968953.abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Although lymph node metastasis is a negative prognostic factor in pancreatic cancer, the significance of non-metastatic lymph node enlargement remains unclear. This study evaluated the prognostic impact of the No. 8 lymph node (N8LN), which is routinely assessed during pancreaticoduodenectomy and identifiable on preoperative imaging. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 99 patients who underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy for pancreatic cancer between 2009 and 2019. The size of the N8LN was measured on preoperative imaging, and patients were divided into small and large groups based on the median value. Long-term oncologic outcomes were compared between the two groups. To assess the local immune response, CD8 immunohistochemistry was performed on nodal sections, and CD8⁺ T-cell density was quantified using QuPath software. RESULTS: The large group showed significantly longer progression-free survival (19.7 vs. 9.4 months) and disease-specific survival (41.7 vs. 17.1 months) than the small group. Enlarged N8LN remained an independent favorable prognostic factor in multivariable analysis. CD8⁺ T-cell density did not differ between groups. CONCLUSION: Enlarge

42965064.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Automated extraction of slide metadata remains a major bottleneck in digital pathology, especially in settings where barcode identifiers are missing, damaged, or inconsistent. Manual transcription of case, block, and stain information is error-prone and does not scale. Building on our previous whole-slide image (WSI)-Babel-Fish framework, we developed WSI-Babel-Shark, a more extensible pipeline for reliable metadata extraction across heterogeneous slide-label layouts. MATERIALS AND METHODS: WSI-Babel-Shark integrates data matrix code decoding, region of interest (ROI)-based optical character recognition (OCR), and rule-based metadata parsing within a modular Python and Docker architecture. To handle diverse institutional label formats, the system incorporates a deep learning-based label layout classifier using a ResNet-18 backbone, fused with handcrafted descriptors and prototype-based open-set recognition to categorize labels into 10 predefined layout groups. A graphical interface supports ROI annotation, dataset management, and configuration editing. Performance was evaluated on 270 WSIs (.svs and .ndpi formats) and cross-validated using 110 slides from the previous

42960345.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models are increasingly applied across the detection, staging, treatment selection, and surveillance of prostate and bladder cancer. Explainable AI links predictions to identifiable features, spatial regions, or architectural constraints, supporting clinical audit and informed use. This narrative review synthesizes evidence across both cancers in imaging, digital pathology, molecular and liquid-biopsy data, and clinical applications and assesses deployment readiness. Two parallel structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE were performed, one for each cancer, covering records through November 15, 2025. Eligible studies applied machine or deep learning to a clinical or translational task and included an explainability component. Seventy studies across 4 data domains were included. Imaging was the most active domain. SHapley Additive exPlanations and gradient-weighted class activation mapping confirmed biologically plausible signal localization. Interpretability-by-design in bladder endoscopy embedded explainability without post hoc approximation.
