42960110.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across the gastric cancer care continuum, but its clinical maturity differs substantially among endoscopy, cross-sectional imaging, digital pathology, prognostic modeling, treatment selection, and surgical support. Existing reviews have often focused on individual modalities or summarized algorithmic performance without systematically distinguishing technical feasibility from translational readiness. We conducted a structured narrative review of studies indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE and the Web of Science Core Collection from January 2022 through July 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking. Earlier landmark studies were retained when necessary to explain the development of major applications. Priority was given to prospective, multicenter, externally validated, and clinically actionable studies. Evidence maturity was assessed according to study design, validation breadth, workflow relevance, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and implementation evidence. The main constraint on gastric cancer AI is no longer pattern-recognition capability but the absence of reproducible clinical benefit under real

42959466.abstract: BACKGROUND: Reliable mitotic identification in whole-slide images (WSIs) is essential for prognostic evaluation and tumor grading; yet, many commercial artificial intelligence (AI) pathology platforms function as opaque black boxes with little auditability and, frequently, little expert supervision throughout development. METHODS: We developed a transparent and repeatable process for mitosis identification using YOLOv8, designed to scale from full slide inference to patch-level benchmarking. Global non-maximum suppression (NMS), GPU accelerated inference, region of interest-driven and adaptive tiling, and tissue gating are all integrated into the pipeline. In order to facilitate expert validation and traceability, audit-ready outputs include detection CSVs, tile manifests, positive and negative overlays, and heatmaps. RESULTS: From small clinical slides (26 tiles, 4 detections) to huge benchmarks (TUPAC SP2 with 14,270 tiles, 1754 detections), six typical WSIs were processed. Whereas throughput averaged 78 tiles/s depending on the slide size and tissue dispersion, average confidence scores remained constant between 0.69 and 0.80. The successful generation of all audit outputs attes

42935755.abstract: Automated whole-slide image (WSI) analysis for cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) is challenged by limited pathological specificity in general models and poor cross-center generalization. We propose CSCC-PAG (pre-training, adaptation, generalization), a framework integrating domain-specific pre-training with self-supervised domain adaptation. Utilizing 8,041 CSCC WSIs, we applied the self-supervised pre-training for CSCC (SPC) feature extractor, which significantly outperforms pan-cancer baselines in the typing, grading, and segmentation tasks. To address domain shift, we developed representative sample domain adaptation (RSDA), combining masked autoencoders (MAEs) with a k-means buffer strategy for label-free adaptation. The results demonstrate that SPC captures fine-grained CSCC morphology, while RSDA effectively recovers performance degradation across centers without requiring target-domain annotations. This study provides a comprehensive solution for automated CSCC diagnosis, covering the entire pipeline from large-scale pre-training to few-shot generalized deployment, demonstrating its immense potential for real-world clinical implementation.

42928519.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) exhibits substantial molecular and morphological heterogeneity, yet current morphology-based prognostic models often lack biological interpretability. We developed a transformer-based computational framework (CTransPath) to virtually predict gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. Morphology-associated genes were identified from the TCGA-HNSC cohort, and a 32-gene morphology-guided prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) based on H&E-derived predicted gene expression was developed using Random Survival Forest and multivariable Cox regression modeling. In TCGA-HNSC, the MGP_HNSC32 risk score significantly stratified patients by progression-free interval (PFI; HR = 4.13, 95% CI: 2.84-6.02), overall survival (OS; HR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.78-3.29), and disease-specific survival (DSS; HR = 4.88, 95% CI: 2.95-8.06; all p < 0.001), and remained independently associated with prognosis after multivariable adjustment. High-risk tumors were enriched for cell cycle, E2F, MYC, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathways and displayed poorly differentiated histology with nuclear atypia and stromal desmoplasia. In contras

42913692.abstract: UNLABELLED: CD73 is an emerging immunotherapy target that is overexpressed in many tumors and generates an adenosine-rich microenvironment to suppress antitumor immunity. In low-grade endometrial carcinoma, CD73 expression varies, and its impact on tumor immunobiology is unknown. Using two microsatellite-stable, grade 2 endometrioid endometrial carcinoma cohorts, in vitro NT5E (CD73) knockout/knockdown, and single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that cancer cell CD73 loss promotes a dual inflammatory and immunosuppressive microenvironment. Cancer cell CD73 loss was associated with increased lymphovascular space invasion and worse recurrence-free and overall survival, whereas stromal CD73 expression did not correlate with outcomes. CD73 downregulation induced pro-inflammatory gene expression, which strongly correlated with upregulation of immunosuppressive genes, including CD274 (PD-L1), suggesting a compensatory mechanism limiting antitumor immunity. Tumors with low cancer cell CD73 exhibited higher PD-L1 expression that correlated with increased CD3+ T-cell infiltration, reflecting an immune-engaged but checkpoint-restrained microenvironment. Single-cell analyses demonstrated t

42904330.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Existing baseline-dependent metastatic breast cancer (MBC) prognostic systems remain limited in capturing tumor evolution under therapeutic pressure. We aimed to develop a dynamic 18F-FDG PET/CT-derived machine learning prognostic model and systematically explore its biological rationale using pathomics and proteomics. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PET metabolic and dynamic biomarkers were extracted from serial baseline and post-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT images of 112 retrospectively included MBC patients. Independent prognostic biomarkers were identified using Cox regression. Prognostic models were constructed through multiple machine learning algorithms, with interpretability provided by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Pathomics (n = 45) and plasma proteomics (n = 48) analyses were performed to characterize risk-associated biological features. RESULTS: Post-treatment metabolic (SUVmax2) and dynamic (ΔSULmax) PET biomarkers emerged as independent prognostic factors for progression-free survival. The final random survival forest model, termed the dynamic PET/CT-based MBC (dPMBC) prognostic model, achieved favorable prognostic stratification, yielding area un

42894874.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in anatomic pathology is dominated by image-based diagnostic applications, but much of the specialty's cognitive work is textual: reviewing clinical history, drafting reports, coordinating testing, and communicating results. Large language models can be useful for many of these tasks, and agentic systems extend their capabilities by retrieving external information, invoking software tools, following task-specific instructions, tracking workflow states, and carrying out complex multi-step tasks under human oversight. This conceptual review outlines key components of agentic AI systems including retrieval augmented generation, tool use, skills, and the so-called "agentic loop"-and applies them to anatomic pathology workflows. Three illustrative design sketches use reflex testing support, workload balancing and case routing, and ancillary test decision support to explain how agentic systems can combine lab information system data, trustworthy knowledge sources, local policy, and explicit human approval gates. We examine considerations for clinical deployment, including interoperability and integration challenges, lifecycle governance and validation, securi

42887393.abstract: Predictive models, as applied in computational pathology, are typically evaluated by accuracy, while their residuals are discarded as errors. In this paper we show that these residuals contain structured biological information. We introduce and validate a conditional discordance framework that uses foundation model prediction residuals to identify tissue regions where morphology and transcriptome diverge. The framework, applied to Xenium spatial transcriptomics data from 18 breast carcinoma sections across 2 cohorts, revealed spatially organized prediction errors with biological associations that varied across patients. In discovery, discordant regions showed higher EPCAM/KRT19 expression and lower expression of several stromal/macrophage markers, while cell mixture associations differed between patients. In two sections of P07, discordant regions enriched in tumor cells showed greater underprediction of transcription associated with EMT after composition adjustment, without a robust increase in observed program expression. Gene predictability is associated with spatial autocorrelation. Observed expression directions agreed across cohorts for 71 of 90 bridge genes; validation pathw

42871743.abstract: Lymphomas comprise a diverse group of heterogeneous cell malignancies, primarily diagnosed through morphological and histochemical analysis of tissue biopsy specimens. Accurate automated nuclear segmentation is essential for quantitative histopathological analysis and downstream computational pathology applications, particularly in morphological heterogeneous lymphoma tissues. In the current study, we used deep learning-based approaches, namely a pre-trained StarDist model, a custom-trained StarDist model, and DeepLabV3, for automated nuclear segmentation of heterogeneous lymphoma cells in histological sections and achieved high accuracy of nuclear segmentation. DeepLabV3 achieved the highest pixel-level segmentation accuracy when trained on large annotated datasets, whereas StarDist demonstrated greater data efficiency under limited training conditions. We next compared the accuracy of nuclear segmentation between conventional formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) specimens and recently proposed glyoxal-based processing of rapidly frozen samples (CRYO). Overall, segmentation performance on CRYO specimens was comparable to that on FFPE specimens, although the magnitude and direct

42871543.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bone marrow reticulin fibrosis is prognostic in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). However, fibrosis assessment is limited by interobserver variability. Computational approaches address this, but remain anchored to qualitative assessment, have limited scalability, and none have explicitly evaluated marrow adiposity. Here we developed a pipeline to predict fibrosis scores using vision-transformer (ViT) models. METHODS: Slide from 643 bone marrow cores from 391 patients with a MPN were digitized and analyzed. Cores were tiled, and Merz grids were overlaid on whole-slide images. Fiber-grid intersections were automatically counted, and ViT models were developed using grid scores as labels. Fat-excluded models were also developed, and sampling strategies were swept. All-length score reflects reticulin intersections relative to all eligible marrow-core grid length, whereas the fat-excluded score reflects reticulin intersections relative to the non-fat eligible marrow compartment. Performance was tested on an unseen patient cohort. RESULTS: Systematic-random sampling of 64 (SR64) tiles per slide had the strongest validation performance across sampling methods, whereas random

42871289.abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have completely transformed the domain of computational pathology (CPath). More specifically, it has altered the diagnostic workflow of pathologists by integrating foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) in their assessment and decision-making process. The limitations of existing deep learning approaches in CPath can be overcome by FMs through learning a representation space that can be adapted to a wide variety of downstream tasks without explicit supervision. Deploying VLMs allow pathology reports written in natural language be used as rich semantic information sources to improve existing models as well as generate predictions in natural language form. In this survey, a holistic and systematic overview of recent innovations in FMs and VLMs in CPath is presented. Furthermore, the tools, datasets, and training schemes for these models are summarized in addition to categorizing them into distinct groups. This extensive survey highlights the current trends in CPath and its possible revolution through the use of FMs and VLMs in the future.

42835573.abstract: Accurate nuclei detection and classification in hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) is a key task in computational pathology, particularly for quantitative analysis of the tumor microenvironment. However, this task remains highly challenging due to variations in nuclei morphology, staining procedures, scanners, organs, magnifications, and WSI artifacts. In addition, many existing pipelines rely on computationally demanding architectures and post-processing procedures, making gigapixel WSI analysis time-consuming. In this work, CellPrior-Net (CP-Net) is proposed, an efficient nuclei detection and classification pipeline that utilizes a lightweight convolutional neural network architecture and hematoxylin (H) channel as prior information to enhance nuclei-aware feature learning. Extensive benchmarking was conducted against state-of-the-art pipelines on eight public and private datasets (total:∼10.4 M nuclei) obtained from different organs, scanners, magnifications, and clinical centers. Experimental results demonstrate that CP-Net achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing inference time. Furthermore, CellQuant-Net was introduced-an end-to-end nucl

42825382.abstract: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by marked spatial immune heterogeneity, commonly manifested as immune‑desert, immune‑excluded and immune‑inflamed phenotypes. These phenotypes are closely associated with variable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Emerging evidence suggests that they are shaped not only by canonical immune pathways but also by mitochondrial processes that regulate immune priming, T‑cell trafficking and the maintenance of effector function. The present review summarizes how mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial DNA‑cGAS‑STING signaling, pathways mediated by tricarboxylic acid cycle metabolites, and non‑cell‑autonomous mitochondrial transfer may contribute to the establishment and maintenance of distinct spatial immune phenotypes in NSCLC. It is proposed that insufficient activation of innate immunity and impaired dendritic cell priming are particularly relevant to immune‑desert tumors, whereas chronic oxidative stress may reinforce barriers mediated by cancer‑associated fibroblasts (CAFs), transforming growth factor β, and the extracellular matrix in immune‑excluded tumors. By contrast, immune‑inflamed tumors may repr

42991642.abstract: BACKGROUND: The landscape of the existing population-based cancer registries (CRs) has evolved significantly in Germany since 2008. This overview article presents the general framework of cancer registration in Germany, with a particular focus on harmonization and standardization of data collection and registration processes. Moreover, it outlines key challenges and limitations and illustrates both current status and future scope of utilization of comprehensive CR data with clinical and epidemiological relevance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Federal and state legislation, resources such as the nationally standardized oncological core dataset for cancer reporting and its technical specifications, jointly developed and maintained by consortia of the CRs and stakeholders, as well as registration recommendations of national and international organizations, have contributed to harmonization, standardization, and validation of data collection and registration processes. RESULTS: The current scope of utilization of CR data is illustrated through a variety of topical examples, including consecutive monitoring of cancer burden on a population level, evaluation of the effectiveness of early detect

42991042.abstract: Neuroimaging research faces five linked barriers: technical complexity, prohibitive costs, lack of transparency, scattered infrastructure, and limited computational resources. Current platforms address these challenges one at a time. As a result, researchers must choose between convenience, transparency, and flexibility. We introduce NeuroStage, a unified, web-based platform that addresses all five barriers together. Technical complexity is removed through a simple interface that requires no programming skills. It supports automatic data upload, anonymisation, organisation of MRI data using the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) format, and standard preprocessing pipelines. Prohibitive costs are addressed through low-cost open access. The platform can be deployed in the cloud or locally, which also allows processing of protected health information with the same user experience. Lack of transparency is resolved through interactive viewers that let researchers check BIDS classification results and quality control reports before preprocessing begins. This prevents wasted computation on low-quality data. Scattered infrastructure is solved by providing a single platform that handles th

42983804.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study demonstrates the use of a locally hosted, offline artificial intelligence approach to identify, quantify, and describe housing-related needs documented in routine case notes from a statewide cancer support service. METHODS: In this retrospective, exploratory service evaluation, a locally hosted, offline large language model screened 25,031 staff-generated case notes recorded between December 2020 and December 2025 for housing-related interactions and grouped confirmed interactions into categories based on a predefined framework. Flagged records and categorisation were independently verified by at least two reviewers, and confirmed interactions were summarised descriptively. RESULTS: Of 25,031 interactions, 308 (1.23%) were confirmed as housing-related interactions. The most prominent categorisations were lack of support from health and social services (44.16%), financial barriers to housing stability (37.66%), and homelessness or reliance on emergency or crisis housing (36.04%). In more than half of confirmed interactions, housing was not the initial reason for contact and emerged only during discussion. CONCLUSIONS: Findings highlight the utility of a privacy

42977355.abstract: Realizing the scientific and clinical potential of large-scale sleep data repositories requires rigorous technical infrastructure for signal processing, quality control, and artificial intelligence (AI) integration. This article addresses the practical implementation steps that follow repository architecture and data ingestion. We outline strategies for linking sleep study data with longitudinal electronic health records, including deterministic and probabilistic matching, temporal alignment, and approaches to handling missing linkages and incomplete clinical data. Finally, we discuss emerging directions, including wearable data integration, federated and privacy-preserving learning, precision medicine applications, and regulatory and health equity considerations essential to responsible repository-scale AI deployment.

42964531.abstract: Digital technologies in healthcare have significantly enhanced clinical decision-making with complex data analysis. However, single clinical centers often lack sufficient data volume or diversity for effective modeling. Distributed learning solutions help to overcome these limitations, and in particular, Swarm Learning (SL) offers a privacy-preserving solution by allowing a decentralized and synchronized model training across multiple centers without direct data sharing. Swarm Learning's inherent focus on data privacy makes it well-suited for distributed healthcare analysis. However, no studies have quantified the impact of an external individual center that wants to join the swarm network in terms of performance and fairness. In this paper, we propose an approach for evaluating the benefits from the point of view of both a new center and the existing swarm network, based on the amount of data introduced by the new center. We also present seven different Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the impact of the new center under different aspects related to the performance variation, model stability, fairness, and quality of the newly introduced data. We apply these indicators

42946016.abstract: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are artificial intelligence models designed to generate novel data that is indistinguishable from real data. Originally developed to generate images to complement existing datasets and create more diverse samples, GAN-based data can enhance downstream analysis for machine learning and deep learning applications. GAN-based approaches are also versatile and suitable for augmenting omics data, improving downstream analyses such as genotype prediction, biomarker detection, and protein de novo design. In addition, GANs can preserve and reconstruct genomic regions under selective pressure, increase sample sizes from underrepresented groups, and mitigate class imbalance effects in genomic analyses, transcriptomics, and single-cell omics. Recent work also demonstrates that GAN-generated data can support privacy-preserving data sharing and the design of novel biological sequences and proteins. This literature review presents the foundational concepts of GANs, explores diverse applications across omics fields, and highlights novel opportunities for applying GAN approaches in livestock genomics.

42831099.abstract: BACKGROUND: Population-based cancer registries rely heavily on the manual coding of unstructured medical reports, a process that is both time-consuming and resource-intensive. The number of cases and reports is increasing and simultaneously qualified coding personnel are rare, making it challenging to maintain timely and high-quality cancer registration. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between March and September 2025, we implemented and evaluated an artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced tool, a modular Python-based application, for tumor data extraction from 82 384 medical reports received by the Eastern Switzerland Cancer Registry. The tool, based on fine-tuned, pretrained German-language bidirectional encoder representations from transformers models, processed reports from >200 institutions, and provided an output file that can be directly integrated into the Swiss cancer registry software NICERStat-KRG (Cantonal Cancer Registries, Switzerland). RESULTS: For 10 739 reports (13%), the incidence date, International Classification of Diseases (ICD) 10 code, and ICD-O-3.2 topography, morphology, and behavior showed complete agreement with the corresponding tumor records in our database. Rema

42828269.abstract: BACKGROUND: Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) is an ultrarare disease characterized by extremely high levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) dysfunction, making most LDLR function-dependent lipid-lowering therapies (LLTs) less effective. For HoFH, LDLR-independent LLTs are usually required to meaningfully reduce LDL-C levels and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. OBJECTIVE: To examine treatment patterns and pathways among people with HoFH. METHODS: A retrospective HoFH cohort was formed using closed claims for evinacumab and lomitapide from the Komodo Healthcare Map® and confirmed diagnoses from myRARE®. myRARE data were de-identified and linked to the Komodo Healthcare Map. LLTs and apheresis at the index date (the last day of the most recent enrollment period) were used to describe contemporary treatment patterns among individuals with HoFH. A reverse Sankey plot described how LLT use evolved over time. RESULTS: In the overall cohort, 15.9% (42/264) did not have LLT claims during the 6 months before and including the index date. At the index date, 42.8% (113/264) of individuals were dispensed LDLR-

42774774.abstract: BACKGROUND: Population-based cancer registries (PBCR) are important for monitoring trends in cancer epidemiology, facilitating the implementation of effective cancer services. Adolescents and young adults (AYAs) with cancer are a group of patients with a unique set of needs. The utility of PBCR in AYAs is limited by the lack of AYA-specific data items. STRONG AYA, an international multidisciplinary consortium, is addressing this through federated learning (FL) methodology and novel data visualisation concepts. A Core Outcome Set has been developed to measure outcomes of importance through clinical data and patient-reported outcomes (PROs). We describe how data from the Yorkshire Specialist Register of Cancer in Children and Young People (YSRCCYP), a PBCR in the UK, is being used within the STRONG AYA and how the subsequent analyses can guide patient consultation through a proof of concept. METHODS: Data from the YSRCCYP were imported into an open-source privacy-enhancing FL infrastructure, from which FL analyses are carried out along with data provided by other consortium members. The results are extracted into the PROMPT software (in-house software developed by the University of L

42705108.abstract: Rapid developments in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) technology have revolutionized healthcare by enabling real-time patient monitoring and remote diagnosis. However, increased connectivity raises significant cybersecurity concerns, such as data breaches, unauthorized access, and potential tampering with medical devices. Techniques such as threat intelligence, log monitoring, and intrusion detection systems are used to identify and respond to cyberattacks on the IoMT. As attackers evolve their strategies, they are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to improve attack detection accuracy. This shift highlights the urgent need for smart, scalable, and privacy-preserving IDS solutions that can protect life-critical medical systems with limited computational resources. This research investigates the use of artificial intelligence (AI), specifically machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and hybrid techniques, to improve intrusion detection systems (IDS) for IoMT security. It includes an overview of publicly available IoMT datasets, an analysis of existing IDS frameworks, and a discussion of the limitations of AI-powered security solutions. Unlike prior surveys tha

42704107.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) has become an important public-health tool for tracking community-level circulation of emerging and re-emerging pathogens, but wastewater measurements are not directly interpretable public-health indicators. Signals recovered from sewer systems are shaped by sampling variability, environmental and inter- and intra-laboratory variations, population-dependent bias, and high-dimensional molecular complexity. Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used to extract predictive and decision-relevant information from these data, but the strength of the supporting evidence varies substantially. This narrative review examines how strongly current applications are supported by published evidence. Sources were identified through iterative searches of three literature-search sources updated to June 2026 and classified by role, analytical task, and strength of evidence. To keep the analytical scope consistent, we use a pragmatic four-layer classification: classical statistical models, conventional machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid or mechanistically informed approaches. Applications are reviewed across five analytical tasks: predictive modelling and fo

42627626.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pharmacotherapy optimization in multimorbid patients is increasingly complex due to polypharmacy, fragmented data, expanding electronic health records, and workforce constraints. Conventional clinical decision support systems remain largely rule-based and often fail to adequately incorporate patient-specific context. While artificial intelligence offers new opportunities, stand-alone models remain insufficiently reliable for high-risk pharmacotherapy decision support. AIM: To develop a relevance-driven, clinician-supervised hybrid AI framework for pharmacotherapy optimization. METHOD: Using a design science-informed approach, an interdisciplinary research group developed a conceptual framework for AI-supported pharmacotherapy optimization. Framework development was informed by prior feasibility work, published literature, clinical practice requirements, and iterative interdisciplinary discussions. Hybrid AI was defined as the combination of retrieval-augmented generation, deterministic safety rules, and large language model reasoning. RESULTS: Seven design principles were identified, including decomposition of clinical activities, relevance-based prioritization, hybri

42569523.abstract: Predicting emotional dysregulation events in children with Autism is essential for timely mitigation of triggering events and prevention of further escalation of the situation. However, there is a scarcity of accessible and standarised datasets for use in AI-based research associated with challenging behaviours in children with ASC. To address this gap, we have curated a novel privacy-preserved dataset as part of an Erasmus+ funded project (AI-TOP-2020-1-UK01-KA201-079,167). The dataset was validated using three machine learning architectures which gave an accuracy of 96% in detecting the affective states related to learning in children with Autism. The key contributions of this study are: 1. Development of an Autism meltdown dataset exemplifies methodological rigor, advances an urgent clinical challenge through early detection and intervention, and enables broad impact by promoting reproducibility, benchmarking and translational health outcomes. 2. Implementation of privacy preserving measures addresses ethical concerns regarding the use of video data with this vulnerable population as part of the machine learning pipeline. 3. High levels of accuracy are demonstrated via empirical

42518655.abstract: Bone is increasingly recognized not as a passive structural scaffold but as a dynamic endocrine organ that secretes a diverse repertoire of bone-derived factors (BDFs) which establish communication axes with the brain, kidney, cardiovascular system, immune network and metabolic organs. Harnessing this endocrine potential for therapy requires technologies that interface with skeletal secretory programs with spatial, temporal and biological precision. Bioactive materials have emerged as a promising platform for this purpose. However, complete examples demonstrating that biomaterials regulate distant organ function through clearly defined BDF-dependent mechanisms remain limited; therefore, this Review discusses biomaterial-based intervention as an emerging framework built on current evidence from local skeletal repair, BDF-related marker regulation and controlled release studies. Concurrently, artificial intelligence may assist osteokine discovery, guiding biomaterial design and enabling patient-specific digital twins of bone-organ axis dynamics. This Review synthesizes current understanding of BDF-mediated inter-organ communication, critically evaluates biomaterial strategies and cli

42518298.abstract: This bibliometric analysis examines the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) research. Using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Bibliometrix, we analyzed 1,938 publications from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015-2026), revealing a dramatic rise in AI-related ICI studies, led by China and the USA. Key findings demonstrate AI's integration in predicting treatment response, optimizing dosing strategies, and managing immune-related adverse events. Through keyword co-occurrence and citation analyses, we identify critical AI applications including digital pathology and tumor microenvironment characterization. This comprehensive overview provides valuable insights into research trends and emerging frontiers for AI-driven innovations in cancer immunotherapy.

42428243.abstract: PURPOSE: The rise of large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4 and DeepSeek has transformed healthcare information processing by enabling natural language-based clinical reasoning. However, the integration of LLMs with privacy-sensitive biomedical signals, particularly electroencephalogram (EEG) data used in brain-computer interface (BCI) systems, remains underexplored. EEG signals, especially during motor imagery (MI) tasks, are critical for assistive neurotechnologies but pose significant privacy risks due to their capacity to reveal cognitive and medical information. Traditional encryption techniques often distort signal structure or require decryption with additional noise, compromising classification performance and real-time usability. METHODS: To address this gap, we propose a deep denoising structure-preserving neural encoding network (DSNet) that enables accurate classification of privacy-preserving encoded EEG representations without requiring decryption. EEG features were extracted using common spatial pattern (CSP) and transformed into privacy-preserving encoded representations while preserving their statistical structure. Here, encoding refers to a non-reversible neur

42263399.abstract: Neural Collapse (NC) is a foundational geometric phenomenon typically observed in the terminal phase of supervised deep network training, where class features converge toward highly symmetric, low-rank structures such as the simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF). While existing literature predominantly characterizes NC as a consequence of label-driven, gradient-based optimization, this work demonstrates that a structurally distinct regime, Bipolar Neural Collapse (BNC), can emerge in a label-free and training-free setting. We propose a fixed-weight multilayer transformation with the computational form of a feedforward network, using top-k selective routing and unit-norm projection on pretrained facial embeddings without learned weights or backpropagation. Our theoretical and empirical analyses reveal that this transformation introduces an inherent low-rank architectural bias that suppresses residual variance and progressively polarizes embeddings into anchor-specific antipodal clusters. The resulting stable and repeatable representations facilitate one-way cryptographic hashing for privacy-preserving face verification without requiring raw facial image storage, backbone retraining,

42212684.abstract: The gut microbiome functions as a key regulator of tumorigenesis and progression, thereby modulating tumor development and treatment outcomes (including chemoresistance, immunotherapy efficacy, and adverse effects) through its influence on the immune microenvironment and metabolite-mediated signaling pathways. Recent advances in multiomics technologies (metagenomics, metabolomics, and transcriptomics) have generated large-scale, comprehensive, and heterogeneous datasets whose complexity exceeds the capabilities of manual analysis, thus necessitating the implementation of artificial intelligence-based approaches. This review systematically examines the crucial role of the gut microbiome in tumorigenesis, with particular emphasis on colorectal cancer (CRC), specifically addressing its utility as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. Furthermore, building upon existing applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in microbiome research and cancer diagnosis and treatment, this review presents an AI-driven precision intervention framework and delineates personalized treatment strategies.

42207498.abstract: Cancer poses a significant threat to human health. The immune response plays a pivotal role in tumor cell elimination, with increasing attention given to the spatiotemporal dynamics of immune cells across temporal, spatial, and functional dimensions. The gut microbiota, which constitutes the majority of the human microbiome, contributes to tumor initiation and progression. The tumor microenvironment (TME) serves as the primary site for immune cell-mediated anti-tumor responses, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites driving immune cell activation and spatiotemporal remodeling. This review explores the mechanisms by which the gut microbiota and its metabolites influence anti-tumor immunity, alongside the impact of immune cell dynamics on tumors. Furthermore, it proposes novel research strategies, including the "gut microbiota-immune cell dynamic monitoring model" and the "organoid-microbe co-culture platform." This work lays a theoretical foundation for advancing our understanding of the underlying mechanisms and developing innovative therapeutic approaches.

42026889.abstract: Hyperglycemia is a major risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD). This multicenter prospective study developed and validated a machine learning (ML) model to predict CKD risk in prediabetic and diabetic populations for early intervention, following TRIPOD+AI guidelines. Participants were enrolled from four communities, with three sites providing training (80%) and internal test (20%) datasets, and the fourth for external validation. Five ML algorithms were constructed, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied to interpret the optimal model. The XGBoost model showed excellent predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.905, 0.809, and 0.837 in training, internal test, and external validation sets, respectively. Serum creatinine (Scr), age, and hemoglobin (Hb) were the leading predictors, with higher Scr, older age, and lower Hb elevating CKD risk. Risk stratification (low: 0%-5%, medium: 5%-25%, high: 25%-100%) yielded distinct CKD incidences of 0.7%, 9.9%, and 55.5% (p < 0.001). An online prediction tool was further established for community screening. This validated ML model enables accurate risk prediction and stratification in hyperglycemic individuals, providing a f

41885802.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into audiology and hearing health, yet evidence from across the health sciences shows that AI systems routinely embed structural biases that can exacerbate inequities, particularly for African and other low- and middle-income country (LMIC) populations. This review identified and analysed bias types in AI applications relevant to audiology and examined their ethical, cultural, and linguistic implications for LMIC settings. A narrative review design was adopted to accommodate the heterogeneity of available evidence, where thematic saturation was more appropriate than effect-size aggregation. Peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025 were retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore, with inclusion requiring explicit engagement with AI and bias or equity. Rigour was assessed using a six-domain quality rubric, and data were extracted into structured evidence tables for thematic synthesis. Thirty-three studies met inclusion criteria: six were audiology-specific empirical studies (all small scale), and the remainder were reviews or conceptual analyses. No study presented empirical African audiogram, a

41834383.abstract: The early detection of chronic kidney disease (CKD) can lead to timely and appropriate clinical intervention. However, most CKD diagnostic systems rely on redundant features and provide unreliable results in small and unbalanced datasets. Therefore, it is challenging to apply them in clinical settings due to a lack of transparency, as well as the extensive amount of time and effort to fine-tune them using manual labor. This article outlines an algorithm to test CKD automatically with a hybrid spiral search strategy-based binary gravitational search algorithm (SSS-BGSA) with elephant herding optimization (EHO) to optimize a Deep Belief Neural Network (DBNN). The code pipeline was designed to involve automated feature selection and model parameter optimization. The objective of using SSS-BGSA in the study was to enhance the exploration-exploitation tradeoff of the original BGSA by a non-linear spiral search pattern. Training of the DBNN using the selected features and optimization of the DBNN parameters were also done using EHO to enhance convergence rate and learning efficiency. The framework was evaluated on the UCI CKD dataset (25 attributes) using nested stratified 5-fold cross-v

41803714.abstract: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common primary glomerulonephritis, requiring improved diagnostic tools. We analyzed three cohorts (GSE37460, GSE93798, and GSE115857 are internal validation cohorts) using gene set enrichment analysis on 7751 pathways. A machine learning model was developed and externally validated in multi-cohort gene expression data (external validation cohorts are GSE99339, GSE116626, and GSE104948). Additionally, immunohistochemistry was performed to validate the expression of key biomarkers and the presence of functionally active immune cells. We developed and validated a multi-cohort machine learning diagnostic model. The selected two-step glmBoost + Enet [alpha = 0.4] model achieved high concordance in GSE37460 (κ = 0.704, p < 0.001), GSE93798 (κ = 0.486, p < 0.001), and GSE115857 (κ = 1.000, p < 0.001). Applying the same model to the external validation cohorts demonstrated strong diagnostic accuracy with AUCs of 0.938 (GSE99339), 0.871 (GSE116626), and 0.926 (GSE104948); the corresponding Kappa statistics were κ = 0.699 (p < 0.001), 0.443 (p = 0.018), and 0.615 (p = 0.023). Nine genes were identified as significant for the diagnosis of IgAN, and HLA-DRA a

41803650.abstract: KDIGO stage-3 acute kidney injury (AKI), a life-threatening complication in critically ill patients with traumatic cervicothoracic spinal cord injury (TCTSCI), was associated with a 49.3% 60-day mortality and a median survival of 20 days in a combined MIMIC-IV/eICU analysis, underscoring its severe clinical consequences and the need for early identification and prediction. To address this need, MedFusion-GP-AKI was developed as a multimodal deep learning framework trained on the MIMIC-IV/eICU cohort and externally validated in 188 patients from four tertiary Chinese centers. Missing data were imputed with a GAN-based method, and key predictors were derived from the original dataset using NOTEARS, variational bottleneck, and adversarial analysis, yielding eleven variables led by lactate, mean arterial pressure, temperature, potassium, and TCTSCI level, with the dataset subsequently balanced using an SMOTified-GAN. Fifteen baseline models were benchmarked under uniform protocols, and the best-performing architectures were integrated into an ensemble that achieved AUCs of 0.938, 0.909, 0.969, 0.945, and 0.921 with APs of 0.841, 0.884, 0.992, 0.927, and 0.878 across pre- and post-SMOTE

41718239.abstract: Culturally appropriate strategies are urgently needed to promote human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination among Chinese gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men. WeChat-based interventions guided by the Information - Motivation - Behavioral Skills (IMB) model offer a theory-driven approach by targeting knowledge, motivation, social norms, and self-efficacy. To evaluate a WeChat-delivered IMB-based intervention designed to improve HPV vaccine acceptability in this population. HPV vaccine acceptability and IMB constructs were assessed at baseline (T0), immediately post-intervention (T1), and 1 month post-intervention (T2). Intervention effects were estimated using generalized estimating equations. Mediation was examined using Hayes' PROCESS macro (Model 4) based on change scores with bootstrapped confidence intervals (CIs). The intervention group reported significantly higher HPV vaccine acceptability at T1 (β = 0.42, 95% CI [0.17, 0.68]; p < .001), although effects attenuated at T2 (β = 0.28, 95% CI [0.00, 0.56]; p = .05). 41321654.abstract: As healthcare text data becomes increasingly complex, it is vital for sentiment analysis to capture local patterns and global contextual dependencies. In this paper, we propose a hybrid Swin Transformer-BiLSTM-Spatial MLP (Swin-MLP) model that leverages hierarchical attention, shifted-window mechanisms, and spatial MLP layers to extract features from domain-specific healthcare text better. The framework is tested on domain-specific datasets for Drug Review and Medical Text, and performance is assessed against baseline models (BERT, LSTM, and GRU). Our findings show that the Swin-MLP model performs significantly better overall, achieving superior metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC) and improving mean accuracy by 1-2% over BERT. Statistical tests to assess significance (McNemar's test and paired t-test) indicate that improvements are statistically significant (p < 0.05), suggesting the efficacy of the architectural innovations. The results' implications indicate that the model is robust, efficiently converges to classification, and is potentially helpful for a wide range of domain-specific sentiment analyses in healthcare. 42999819.abstract: Precision oncology has transformed cancer care globally through biomarker-driven and genomically guided treatment strategies. In Asia, where nearly 60% of the world's population resides, the implementation of molecular profiling presents both significant opportunities and unique challenges. Despite increasing adoption, precision diagnostics remain largely concentrated in urban and academic centers, with disparities in access, infrastructure, and expertise across the region. Advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS), including targeted gene panels, comprehensive genomic profiling, whole exome sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing, have enabled the identification of actionable alterations across multiple tumor types. Liquid biopsy approaches, including circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and circulating tumor cells (CTCs), are further transforming cancer care by enabling real-time disease monitoring and detection of resistance mechanisms. Integration of multiomics platforms is increasingly enhancing clinical decision-making. Molecular tumor boards play a critical role in interpreting complex genomic data and facilitating genomically guided treatment decisions, including targeted thera

42999809.abstract: Precision oncology is redefining cancer therapeutics worldwide. In Australia, the integration of genomic medicine into routine clinical oncology remains inconsistently constrained by fragmented funding mechanisms, regional disparities, and a limited workforce. Understanding these structural and policy challenges is crucial for transitioning toward a sustainable, equitable genomic health ecosystem. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from national policy frameworks, peer-reviewed literature, and translational oncology initiatives to examine the current state of precision oncology in Australia. Key domains of analysis include clinical practice patterns, access and equity, infrastructure, data governance, regulatory oversight, and health-policy reform. Although major initiatives, such as Omico's Precision Oncology Screening Platform Enabling Clinical Trials (PrOSPeCT) platform, the ZERO Childhood Cancer Program, and the forthcoming national coordination body Genomics Australia, demonstrate substantial progress, significant implementation barriers persist. Australia stands on the cusp of realizing a genomics-enabled model of cancer care. Consolidation of national governance unde

42999357.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Since its pivotal introduction in 2011, gadoxetic acid has fundamentally revolutionized the landscape of hepatobiliary imaging in China, shifting the diagnostic paradigm from morphological assessment toward functional hepatocyte-level evaluation. This review comprehensively summarizes its 15-year clinical evolution within the Chinese healthcare system, exploring its pharmacological benefits, advanced applications, and future integration with data-driven frameworks. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, spanning from 2011 to 2026. The search targeted peer-reviewed articles, consensus statements, clinical guidelines, and high-impact reviews published in English and Chinese regarding gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Gadoxetic acid provides high sensitivity for early small hepatocellular carcinoma (sHCC) detection via specific OATP1B3 uptake. Beyond lesion detection, its quantitative mapping shows potential for estimating hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and risk stratificatio

42997936.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases such as colorectal cancer and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) contribute substantially to global morbidity, with colorectal cancer accounting for nearly 10% of all cancer diagnoses worldwide. Many existing artificial intelligence (AI) models suffer from limited generalizability and poor clinical interpretability. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an explainable AI (XAI) framework for classifying GI diseases from endoscopic images. METHODS: Public datasets from the Simula Research Laboratory were used: Hyper-Kvasir (10,662 images) for training, Kvasir-V1 (4,000 images) for validation, and Kvasir-V2 (8,000 images) as an independent test set. Two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, GastroNet-dilated multi-scale attention (DMSA) (a proposed DMSA Network) and M2ShallowNet (a lightweight hybrid model), were designed for complementary feature extraction. Deep features were fused using a dual context attentive feature network (DCAF-Net) followed by Aquila Optimizer (AO)-based feature-weight refinement without introducing additional trainable fusion parameters. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-sco

42993876.abstract: BACKGROUND: Socially assistive robots are increasingly explored in health care, but evidence from routine pediatric outpatient settings remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This study examined how contextual support and human facilitation shaped visitor interaction with the Temi V3 robot and which sociotechnical conditions were associated with practical acceptance according to staff. METHODS: A mixed methods pilot combined structured behavioral observation across baseline, poster support, and staff facilitation conditions with 4 staff focus group interviews. The observation unit was a visitor passage through the lobby zone; the qualitative sample comprised 12 staff members with direct exposure to the robot. Quantitative indicators were analyzed descriptively, and staff interviews underwent deductive-inductive qualitative content analysis. RESULTS: In total, 675 visitor passages (children: n=398, 59% and adults: n=277, 41%) were recorded (baseline: n=257; poster support: n=160; and staff facilitation: n=258). Looking at the robot increased from 8 (3.1%) passages at baseline to 30 (18.8%) with poster support and 80 (31%) with staff facilitation. Screen or app use increased from 2 (0.8%) passa

42993695.abstract: Falls among older adults represent a major public health concern with substantial clinical, societal, and economic implications. People living with dementia (PlwD) are disproportionately affected, reflecting the combined impact of cognitive, motor, and pharmacological vulnerabilities. Traditional fall risk assessment tools have demonstrated limitations in capturing the complex, dynamic risk profiles of people living with dementia, highlighting the need for technological innovation in prediction, detection, and prevention. Despite advances in gerontechnology, evidence specific to dementia remains limited. To address this gap, a scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. Comprehensive searches across Scopus, Medline, Embase, APA PsycINFO, and CINAHL identified thirteen peer-reviewed studies (2015-2025) evaluating technology-based approaches for fall prediction, detection, or prevention among people living with dementia or populations used to model dementia-related functional impairments. Data were extracted and synthesized thematically by technological function. Thirteen studies met inclusion criteria, encompassing pressure-sensitive pla

42992946.abstract: PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to neuroimaging, electrophysiology, clinical text, and digitally measured behavior, but reported performance often exceeds the maturity of clinical evidence. METHOD: We conducted a structured narrative review, informed by SANRA principles, of English-language human studies, reviews, and regulatory sources identified in PubMed/MEDLINE and IEEE Xplore from January 2022 through July 2026; older landmark studies were retained when necessary for historical or methodological context. We applied a common translational-evidence framework across six prespecified neurological domains to distinguish technical performance from external validation, prospective clinical evaluation, implementation, and demonstrated patient benefit. Evidence was appraised according to cohort representativeness, patient-level data separation, external and prospective validation, calibration, clinical comparators, regulatory status, workflow integration, and patient-level benefit. 42992786.abstract: The fragmentation of sensitive medical data across institutions and stringent privacy regulations creates isolated data silos, hindering the development of robust AI-driven healthcare solutions. Existing approaches often lack sufficient trust mechanisms, comprehensive auditability, and dynamic access control for multi-center collaboration. Goal: This protocol aims to resolve the tension between collaborative utility and data sovereignty by integrating federated learning (FL) with blockchain technology, providing a secure, auditable, and scalable framework for medical data sharing. The framework employs a tripartite architecture: cryptographic FL with adaptive regularization and Paillier homomorphic encryption for privacy-preserving local training; a multi-channel, tiered-sharding blockchain for decoupled access control, data provenance, and FL operation logging; and a dynamic privacy-computation coordination mechanism that adapts differential privacy and cryptographic protocols based on data sensitivity and hardware capability. 42991056.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term data for digital therapeutics in urinary incontinence are scarce. We assessed whether improvements with app-based multimodal therapy are sustained over 48 weeks, and outcomes after a 12-week delay in initiation. METHODS: In this prespecified 48-week follow-up of the DINKS (Digital Incontinence Study) randomised waitlist-controlled trial, women (≥18 years) with stress, urge, or mixed urinary incontinence recruited between April 30 and September 2 2024 across Germany received app-based therapy immediately or after a 12-week waitlist, alongside standard care. The primary outcome was change from baseline in ICIQ-UI-SF (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Urinary Incontinence Short Form) score at weeks 12, 24, 36, and 48. Trial registration: NCT06389838. FINDINGS: Data availability declined progressively from 186 of 194 participants (95.9%) at week 12-66 (34.0%) at week 48. Pooled improvements exceeded the minimal clinically important difference at 12, 24, and 36 weeks after therapy start (ICIQ-UI-SF at 36 weeks -4.13, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) -4.80 to -3.47), and 73-77% of participants met the responder threshold. 42990691.abstract: Accurate discrimination of benign and malignant breast lesions is essential for early diagnosis, yet remains challenging due to lesion heterogeneity and interobserver variability in ultrasound assessment. We developed a deep learning (DL) framework integrating dual inverted bottleneck blocks (Dual-IB), adaptive hierarchical feature fusion, and knowledge distillation (KD) for breast ultrasound lesion classification. The model was trained and evaluated on public datasets and validated on an independent external cohort to assess its generalizability. Results demonstrated superior performance compared with baseline methods and resident radiologists, while maintaining robust performance across diverse datasets and imaging conditions. On the external validation dataset, the model achieved the best performance, with an accuracy (Acc) of 92.64% and an F1-score of 92.37%. Furthermore, class activation mapping (CAM) visualizations revealed focused and anatomically plausible attention patterns within lesion regions, aiding interpretation and suggesting its potential to assist in breast ultrasound lesion classification.

42986569.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) is the most common biliary tract malignancy and is usually diagnosed at an advanced stage. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly applied to its diagnosis, surgical management and prognostication, but how far the reported performance can be trusted is unclear. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 5 May 2026 using database-specific search strategies. Each primary prediction-model study was characterized separately by design, number of centers and validation type (internal, temporal or external). RESULTS: Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. 42999753.abstract: CT-guided microcoil localization facilitates minimally invasive resection of small pulmonary nodules, but intravascular migration is rare and potentially serious. A 63-year-old man with treated classical Hodgkin lymphoma underwent localization of an FDG-avid right upper lobe semisolid nodule before planned video-assisted thoracoscopic resection. Cone-beam CT showed a 7.6 × 19.1 mm lesion 37.3 mm from the pleura. With the patient supine, a 0.7 mm × 5 cm Visicoil marker was deployed once through a 10 cm, 18-gauge coaxial needle positioned 2.7 mm from the lesion. No pleural anchoring was used, and vascular puncture was not recognized. Immediate fluoroscopy and cone-beam CT showed no coil at the target and a small tract hematoma; short-interval imaging demonstrated changing cardiac-vascular projections. The procedure was aborted. Echocardiography did not visualize the coil or show thrombus, valvular interaction, or new myocardial injury. Dedicated cardiac CT was interpreted as showing the coil along the inferior right ventricular wall, but the discordant earlier nongated images prevented reconstruction of a physiologic migration route. 42999659.abstract: The identification of strategies that improve participant enrollment in clinical trials remains a key focus of stakeholders in this field, due to its role as a leading indicator of timely trial completion and its contributions to the validity and generalizability of clinical trial results. The VA Cooperative Studies Program (CSP) Network of Dedicated Enrollment Sites (NODES) replicated a previously piloted research site mentorship model in two actively enrolling CSP-funded clinical trials to validate its impact on study participant enrollment (CSP #2005: VA Lung Cancer Surgery vs. Stereotactic Radiotherapy trial (VALOR) and CSP #2008: Pentoxifylline in Diabetic Kidney Disease (VA PTXRx)). The "Total Randomized Participants (#) by Mentee Site" and the "Percentage of Randomized Participants (Actual/Expected) Monthly Average By Site (%)" were evaluated across participating mentee study sites over three time periods: 1) 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP), 2) 5-month intervention period (IP), and 3) 3-month follow-up period (FUP). These data were averaged across months during the respective time periods (PIP, IP, FUP). Our findings demonstrate an association between the NODES site me

42999649.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pathological vertebral compression fractures from spinal tumors are a source of severe back pain and functional disability. Vertebral augmentation (VA) has been utilized for mechanical stabilization; however, pain may persist due to nociceptive signaling from the basivertebral nerve (BVN). BVN radiofrequency ablation (BVNRFA) has shown efficacy for vertebrogenic back pain associated with Modic changes, but its efficacy for oncologic/pathologic fractures remains an area of exploration. CASE PRESENTATION: We present a case series of three patients with pathological vertebral compression fractures secondary to spinal tumors who underwent concurrent BVNRFA and VA. All three patients experienced immediate and sustained pain reduction with improvements in function. No peri- or post-procedural complications were observed at one-month follow-up. CONCLUSION: Concurrent BVNRFA and VA is a novel and synergistic approach that may provide an additional option for select patients with pathological vertebral compression fractures from a spinal tumor within palliative and interventional pain settings. Larger studies are required to clarify ideal patient selection, duration of benefit

42997573.abstract: Respiratory motion management is essential in particle therapy because dose distributions are highly sensitive to motion. This study aimed to clarify the current implementation and technical trends of respiratory motion management in particle therapy in Japan. A questionnaire was distributed to all particle therapy facilities in Japan. Responses were received from 16 of the 26 institutions surveyed (61.5%). The survey investigated treatment sites requiring respiratory motion management, CT datasets used for treatment planning, irradiation techniques, respiratory monitoring devices, gating phase determination methods, dose evaluation approaches, and patient positioning techniques. The liver and pancreas were the treatment sites most frequently managed with respiratory motion mitigation, with 81.3% (13/16) of facilities implementing motion management for both sites. The most commonly used CT dataset for treatment planning was end-expiration phase CT (56.3%, 9/16). End-expiration respiratory-gated irradiation was the most commonly used irradiation method (87.5%, 14/16), while free-breathing and breath-hold irradiation were used less frequently. 42997015.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify latent profiles of comprehensive needs among patients with gastrointestinal cancer receiving chemotherapy and examine factors associated with profile membership. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 341 adults with gastrointestinal cancer receiving chemotherapy at a tertiary hospital in Qingdao, China, from October 2024 to June 2025. Participants completed the Comprehensive Needs Assessment Tool in Cancer (CNAT), Strategies Used by People to Promote Health, Family APGAR Index, Comprehensive Scores for Financial Toxicity based on Patient-Reported Outcome Measures, and Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form. Latent profile analysis was conducted using the eight CNAT domain scores. Factors associated with profile membership were examined using multinomial logistic regression with the three-step approach. RESULTS: Three profiles were identified based on most likely class membership: low needs-information priority group (38.1%), moderate needs-balanced group (40.5%), and high needs-medical priority group (21.4%). 42996579.abstract: Primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL) is a rare thyroid malignancy that may present with respiratory symptoms overlapping with cardiopulmonary disease, contributing to delayed diagnosis. We report a 78-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, and prior lung cancer whose worsening dyspnea was repeatedly attributed to underlying cardiopulmonary conditions. She subsequently developed dysphonia and dysphagia with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass requiring tracheostomy for airway protection. Prior computed tomography imaging obtained during multiple evaluations for cardiopulmonary symptoms incidentally demonstrated subtle thyroid enlargement with progressive interval growth on retrospective review. Core biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and staging established stage IIIE disease. Given her age and comorbidities, a dose-reduced regimen of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone was initiated. Despite treatment, her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she died shortly thereafter. This case underscores how overlapping comorbidities can obscure PTL presentation until advanced airway compro

42991466.abstract: Rapid tests will likely become increasingly available to crime scene investigators and have the potential to fundamentally change how decisions are made during the examination of the crime scene. By speeding up the analysis of traces, preliminary results from on-site rapid testing can already be used to support decision-making at the crime scene and may ultimately transform how crime scenes are examined. However, crime scene investigators' decision-making remains influenced by cognitive factors that also affect current examination practices. Given the lack of practical guidance on decision-making in guidelines and forensic science handbooks, it is essential to understand how crime scene investigators make decisions in practice. In this scoping literature review (N = 32), we examine how crime scene investigators search for, interpret, collect, and analyse traces, and how the introduction of rapid tests may influence these decision-making processes. The review reveals that guidelines and handbooks have paid little attention to cognitive factors that may shape investigators' observations and decisions. Empirical studies, however, show that cognitive factors play an important role in t

42990759.abstract: Upper Northern Thailand experiences recurrent seasonal PM2.5 pollution, particularly during periods of biomass burning. This study assessed the spatial and seasonal distribution of ambient PM2.5 concentrations and health risks across eight provinces during 2021-2023. Non-carcinogenic risk was evaluated using hazard quotients (HQs) relative to PM2.5 benchmarks established by the World Health Organization (WHO), the U.S. National Ambient Air Quality Standards (U.S. NAAQS), and Thailand's National Environment Board (NEB) standards. The regional mean (± SD) PM2.5 concentration was 27.57 ± 23.40 µg/m3 (range, 8.40-78.64 µg/m3). Mean HQs were higher in the dry season than in the rainy season, increasing from 1.19 ± 0.23-4.31 ± 1.22 for WHO guidelines, from 0.50 ± 0.10-1.80 ± 0.51 for U.S. NAAQS, and from 0.24 ± 0.05-0.86 ± 0.24 for NEB standards. The PM2.5 concentrations and HQs varied greatly among provinces and seasons, with the highest values in the dry season. The results show that there are large differences in space and time of PM2.5 exposure in Upper Northern Thailand, and the dry season is the time of greatest exposure. 42990737.abstract: As the antitumor mechanism of oridonin has not been clearly demonstrated, the effect of programmed cell death protein 4 (PDCD4) regulated by microRNA (miR)-155-5p on the proliferation of leukemia cells after exposure to oridonin was detected. Regarding the cell cycle profile, there was downregulation of the S phase, upregulation of the G2/M phase and no significant change in the G0/G1 phase. The downregulation of miR-155-5p was demonstrated by the differentially gene chromatin immunoprecipitation and verified using RT-qPCR in HL60 cells treated with oridonin. Compared with the oridonin group, the expression of miR-155-5p was restored after co-transfection of miRNA-155-5p mimics with oridonin, and the miR-55-5p inhibitor significantly downregulated the expression of miR-155-5p compared with the control group. 42986194.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the performance of Sybil, a Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI)-based nodule model, and their combination for 1-year lung cancer detection in two screening cohorts: the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) and the Pamplona International Early Lung Cancer Action Program (P-IELCAP). Materials and Methods Baseline low-dose CT (LDCT) examinations from the NLST and the P-IELCAP were analyzed. A prespecified OR-stacked composite model combining Sybil, a MONAI-based nodule model, and a safety-net rule (MONAI-detected nodule > 6 mm with detection confidence > 0.95) was developed and evaluated for 1-year lung cancer detection. Model discrimination was assessed by using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and operating-point performance metrics were calculated. 42985846.abstract: BACKGROUND: Targeted lung cancer screening programmes in the United Kingdom use multivariable risk models to identify high-risk individuals. However, public acceptability of targeting screening by risk using eligibility criteria, such as age and smoking history, remains unclear, including the psychological and behavioural consequences of eligibility disclosure. AIM: To explore UK public attitudes toward the acceptability of current risk-based eligibility criteria for lung cancer screening and the anticipated psychological and behavioural responses to eligibility disclosure. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted as the second phase of a sequential explanatory design. Semi-structured telephone interviews were held with 28 UK adults aged 45-77 years between January-April 2024. Participants were purposively sampled for diversity in demographics, smoking history, and prior acceptability questionnaire responses. Interviews were analysed using applied thematic analysis informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. RESULTS: Criteria were generally acceptable when perceived as evidence-based and logical, particularly age and smoking history. However, participants expected fle

42974276.abstract: The association between inflammation and cancer has been extensively studied. However, studies examining the relationship between the magnitude of inflammatory fluctuations and cancer remain limited. Consequently, the present study aimed to explore the association between high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) variability and the occurrence of cancer. A total of 42,514 participants were enrolled in the present study, with their hs-CRP levels measured over a 4-year period. The coefficient of variation (CV) of hs-CRP was used to quantify the variability in inflammatory status. Cox regression analysis was used to assess the association between hs-CRP variability and cancer risk after adjusting for potential confounding factors. The results demonstrated that a high CV of hs-CRP was significantly associated with reduced cancer risk [hazard ratio (HR), 0.84; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.75-0.94]. Participants with high hs-CRP and low CV had a significantly increased risk of cancer (HR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.18-1.70). 42973940.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma is among the most common malignancies in the United States and accounts for ~5% of all cancers. Melanoma preferentially metastasizes to lymph nodes, lungs, liver and brain, while bladder involvement is rare and associated with poor prognosis. The present study reports a 79-year-old woman with stage III, operable, BRAF wild-type melanoma of the back, treated with surgical excision and adjuvant immunotherapy. During adjuvant pembrolizumab treatment, a first solitary pulmonary relapse was observed. The metastasis was amenable to surgical resection, and the patient continued immunotherapy. Subsequently, recurrent haematuria led to the identification of a bladder lesion, which was removed via transurethral resection and the pathological evaluation confirmed metastatic melanoma. Following this second relapse, restaging imaging documented systemic disease progression involving lymph nodes, liver and bone. The patient then initiated first-line treatment with nivolumab and ipilimumab, achieving an ongoing clinical and radiological partial response. This study highlights several clinically relevant aspects: The potential role of local treatment strategies for oligoprogress

42967198.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Extreme thrombocytosis (EXT; platelet count >1000 × 109/L) is a rare haematological abnormality that may be primary or reactive. Data on its incidence and management in patients with malignancy are limited. We retrospectively evaluated the incidence, management, and complications of EXT in patients with malignancy over a 12-year period. METHODS: Two-hundred and twenty patients with malignancy experienced at least one episode of EXT during the study period. Patients with a known or subsequent diagnosis of myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) were excluded from analysis. Clinical data were collected from electronic patient records. RESULTS: We identified 198 patients (57% female), with a median age of 55 years (range 1-86) and median follow-up of 55 months. The median peak platelet count was 1112 × 109/L (range 1001-2593). Most patients (77%) had solid tumours, lung cancer being most common (25%). MPN screening was performed in 11 patients (5.5%), with no positive results. Thrombocytosis resolved in 70% but persisted in 28%. Antiplatelets were prescribed in 16% and anticoagulation in 18%, almost exclusively for venous thrombosis. 42965526.abstract: Some patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) progress at a few sites while disease elsewhere stays controlled, a pattern consistent with focal, oligo-acquired immune escape rather than systemic treatment failure. Ablating the escaping focus may eliminate the resistant clone and preserve an otherwise effective immunotherapy line. We performed a PRISMA 2020-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of local ablative treatment (LAT) for oligoprogressive or oligo-resistant metastatic NSCLC during active ICI therapy, with continuation of the same immunotherapy line after LAT. MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 8, 2026. From 1270 records, 22 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Four studies, one randomized subgroup, and three retrospective cohorts contributed to each primary analysis. LAT-oriented management was associated with improved progression-free survival (PFS; pooled hazard ratio [HR] 0.45, 95% CI 0.33-0.62; 95% prediction interval [PI] 0.28-0.74; I2 = 0%) and overall survival (OS; po

42961781.abstract: Adenosine deaminase acting on RNA 1 (ADAR1) has emerged as an important cancer dependency and suppressor of innate immunity. While early therapeutic strategies focused on global enzymatic inhibition, these approaches may compromise essential homeostatic functions of the constitutively expressed ADAR1-p110 isoform. Growing evidence highlights editing-independent functions uniquely mediated by the interferon-inducible ADAR1-p150 isoform. Through its conformation-specific Zα domain, ADAR1-p150 binds Z-nucleic acids and suppresses MDA5-, PKR-, and ZBP1-driven innate immune activation, thereby promoting tumor immune evasion and adaptation to inflammatory stress. Consequently, selectively disrupting this p150-mediated suppression may represent a more therapeutically tractable strategy than global ADAR1 inhibition, with the Zα domain providing a potentially selective mechanistic interface. This review synthesizes current understanding of Zα-mediated immune regulation, evaluates emerging domain-specific therapeutic approaches, and provides a comprehensive guide to the biophysical and cell-based assays used to interrogate Zα interactions, highlighting key mechanistic gaps that may inform fu

42959795.abstract: Pancreatic metastases from lung cancer are uncommon and may be difficult to distinguish from primary pancreatic malignancies. We report 2 patients with lung cancer and pancreatic lesions causing biliary obstruction. The first patient was a 58-year-old man with small-cell lung carcinoma and a pancreatic head mass associated with biliary and pancreatic duct dilatation and extensive vascular contact. Endoscopic ultrasound demonstrated a heterogeneous hypoechoic mass, and endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition confirmed a pancreatic metastasis from pulmonary small-cell carcinoma. The patient underwent endoscopic biliary drainage followed by cisplatin and etoposide chemotherapy. The second patient was a 61-year-old man with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma and a progressively enlarging pancreatic head lesion. Two endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspirations performed 1 month apart were nondiagnostic. The patient subsequently developed obstructive jaundice caused by a severe distal common bile duct stricture.
