42956631.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Breast cancer molecular subtype determination is crucial for personalized treatment planning but currently relies on expensive gene expression profiling or immunohistochemistry with discordance rates up to 30%. This study presents a systematic comparison of context-awareness mechanisms for molecular subtype prediction directly from H&E whole-slide images, evaluating graph-based spatial modeling against attention-based aggregation across multiple architectures, datasets, and deployment scenarios. METHODS: The WSI2Graph framework is adapted to represent whole-slide images as spatial KNN graphs, enabling a controlled comparison of context-aware (CA) graph convolutional aggregation against non-context-aware (NCA) attention-based pooling under identical feature extraction. Three evaluation protocols (EP1-EP3) assess within-domain performance (EP1; BCNB dataset, 1058 core-needle biopsies), constrained cross-domain transfer (EP2; SBC dataset, 533 surgical resection specimens), and foundation model integration (EP3; CONCH), all validated with McNemar's paired tests. 42863187.abstract: Prognostic assessment via whole-slide images (WSIs) is a key task in computational pathology. However, the development of robust predictive models is often bottlenecked by the scarcity of survival-annotated data, given the longitudinal nature of clinical follow-up. Despite its potential, semi-supervised learning (SSL) remains underexplored in this field. Existing SSL methods, primarily designed for natural image classification, rely on the assumption of marginally independent categories, which makes them difficult to adapt to the high-dimensional complexity of WSIs and the temporal continuity inherent in survival outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel semi-supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) framework tailored for WSI-based prognosis. Specifically, we first introduce a morphology-perceived MIL network (Morph-MIL) that jointly models tissue composition and global semantic representations. To maintain a stable reference, a dynamic memory bank is employed to encapsulate the multi-level representations of labeled samples (censored & uncensored). Furthermore, we develop a pseudo-labeling strategy that assigns discrete labels containing temporal relationships to annotat

42809995.abstract: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is one of the most common cancer subtype, with an increasing incidence and a significant impact on cancer-related mortality. SCC grading using whole slide images is inherently challenging due to the lack of a standardized grading protocol and substantial tissue heterogeneity. We propose RACR-MIL, a weakly-supervised SCC grading approach that achieves robust generalization across multiple anatomies (skin, head & neck, lung). RACR-MIL is an attention-based multiple-instance learning framework that introduces two key innovations for learning grade-specific contextual representations: (1) a hybrid WSI graph that captures both local tissue context and non-local phenotypic dependencies between tumor regions, and (2) rank-ordering constraints on the attention mechanism that encourage consistent prioritization of higher-grade tumor regions and improves region-level grade confidence, aligning with pathologists' diagnostic process. Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple SCC datasets, achieving 3%-9% improvements over existing methods and up to 10% improvement in tumor localization. In a pilot study, pathologists reported that RACR-MIL im

42839367.abstract: Enterovirus 2B is a highly conserved, functionally versatile, nonstructural protein. The classic viroporin model, which restricts its role to ion channel formation, cannot account for its interactions with host factors such as Bcl-2-associated X protein, interleukin enhancer-binding factor 2, and karyopherin subunit alpha 1, nor its functional divergence among enteroviruses. We propose a novel, testable membrane stress sensor hypothesis: the transmembrane helices of 2B sense lipid composition and pH changes, and through conformational dynamics, spatiotemporally coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis, and immune evasion. We elaborate on this framework across six dimensions: structure-function mapping, calcium signaling, cell death pathways, immune evasion, evolutionary footprint, and antiviral targeting, along with cross-virus comparisons. We highlight key evidence gaps and limitations, and propose several future research directions. This framework establishes a mechanistic foundation for understanding 2B function and guiding rational anti-enteroviral drug designs.

42947979.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The environmental impact of endoscopic techniques remains poorly defined. We compared procedure-related environmental outcomes between conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) and underwater EMR (U-EMR) for colorectal lesions. METHODS: In this prospective pilot procedure-based life cycle assessment of the resection phase, 10-25-mm colorectal lesions underwent EMR or U-EMR across three endoscopy units. Outcomes included global warming potential (GWP, kg CO2-equivalent/procedure), waste, life-cycle water consumption, fossil resource scarcity, and terrestrial acidification. Exploratory GWP per en bloc resection was estimated using pooled randomized-trial and pilot-cohort data. RESULTS: Forty-nine procedures were included: 23 EMR and 26 U-EMR. En bloc resection was achieved in 56.5% of EMR and 69.2% of U-EMR, and R0 resection in 52.2% and 69.2%. Mean GWP was significantly lower with U-EMR than EMR (1.92 ± 0.54 vs. 2.42 ± 0.50 kg CO2-eq; p = 0.002), corresponding to a reduction of 0.50 kg CO2-eq per procedure and 50 kg CO2-eq per 100 procedures. U-EMR was associated with lower waste generation (324.0 ± 78.3 vs. 407.3 ± 72.0 g; p < 0.001), water consumption (0.56 ± 0.1

42923600.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Sustainable development oals in gastrointestinal endoscopy (GIE), referred to as "green endoscopy," have been a research focus in Western countries. However, the environmental burden of GIE in Japan is poorly understood. We quantify medical waste and estimate GIE-derived incineration-related CO2 emissions in Japan. METHODS: In a dual-center observational study, we report waste from esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), colonoscopy (CS), endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), and endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) from June 2024 to January 2025. We classify waste as infectious/non-infectious, combustible/non-combustible, liquid, or sharps. We record the per-procedure waste and the procedure time, estimate CO2 emissions from the combustion of the measured waste mass using combustion equations for cellulose and polyethylene, and calculate per-minute emissions and annual totals. Sensitivity analyses are performed for changes in the anticipated waste composition. RESULTS: Estimated per-procedure CO2 emissions are 949, 1178, 5834, and 4780 g for EGD, CS, ESD, and ERCP, respectively. Aggregate per-minute emissions are 168, 165, 89, and 75 g/min for ERCP, EGD, C

42824459.abstract: Flushing endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a refinement of saline immersion ESD in which energy-synchronized saline flushing from the knife tip is hypothesized to disperse micro-bubbles and facilitate more controlled coagulation at the tissue interface. We retrospectively evaluated the technical feasibility of this approach in 10 rectal procedures performed at a tertiary referral center. Complete procedural videos were reviewed to describe treated visible submucosal vessel burden, minor bleeding, episodes of transient loss of visualization, and hemostatic forceps use. En bloc and histologically margin-negative (R0) resection was achieved in all 10 cases, while curative endoscopic resection was achieved in nine cases (90%). No intraprocedural perforation, delayed bleeding, post-ESD coagulation syndrome, or unplanned repeat intervention occurred. Median lesion size was 55 mm (interquartile range, 40-69.5), median procedure duration was 102.5 min (100-167.5), and median treated visible vessel count was 21 (11.5-40.75), corresponding to 1.04 vessels/cm2 (0.64-1.74). Minor bleeding and transient loss of visualization occurred during procedures but were controlled endoscopically.

42732378.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Japan NBI Expert Team (JNET) Type 1 classification is used for optical characterization of colorectal lesions with magnifying NBI, but reported Type 1-related findings may differ between readers when assessing serrated lesions. This small-scale post hoc reader-based study explored reported feature-classification patterns associated with JNET Type 1 selection among serrated colorectal lesions and compared them between expert and non-expert endoscopists. METHODS: We analyzed de-identified data from two web-based image-interpretation studies using the same colorectal lesion image dataset. Thirteen histologically confirmed serrated lesions (11 sessile serrated lesions [SSLs] and two hyperplastic polyps [HPs]) assessed by 27 expert and 49 non-expert Japanese endoscopists were included. Simplified JNET responses were dichotomized as Type 1 versus non-Type 1. Classification and regression tree analysis was used to visualize associations between this outcome and predefined features, including Type 1-supportive findings and an anti-Type 1 composite variable. Variability was assessed using entropy. RESULTS: In the expert and non-expert core models, the root splits were anti-Type

42707595.abstract: Superficial non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors (SNADETs) are increasingly treated with endoscopic resection. Although conventional thermal techniques are effective, the thin duodenal wall and distinctive anatomy have driven interest in cold resection techniques that avoid electrocautery-related injury. This narrative review individually appraises cold snare polypectomy (CSP), cold forceps polypectomy (CFP), and cold snare endoscopic mucosal resection (CS-EMR) for duodenal SNADETs. Management of selected small low-grade adenomas should be individualized, with careful surveillance considered as an alternative to immediate resection. When resection is chosen, CSP is the principal cold resection technique for lesions <10 mm that are optically diagnosed as low-grade adenomas using white-light imaging and narrow-band imaging. CSP appears technically feasible and safe for selected small SNADETs. However, its shallow resection depth limits vertical margin assessment. Available follow-up data suggest low recurrence rates, and recurrent lesions are generally small and endoscopically manageable. This review also discusses the importance of pretreatment optical diagnosis, appropriate les

42694724.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Covered self-expandable metal stents (SEMS) are widely used for treating distal malignant biliary obstruction (MBO). Severe SEMS angulation can cause stent dysfunction. Placement of a long double-pigtail plastic stent inside the SEMS (the "long-anchoring stent method") may straighten the angulated SEMS, thereby achieving effective biliary drainage. This study aimed to report the clinical outcomes of this novel method. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 15 patients with distal MBO who underwent initial SEMS placement, subsequently experienced clinical failure or early recurrent biliary obstruction (RBO) within 90 days of initial placement, and underwent reintervention with the long-anchoring stent method between April 2020 and March 2025. RESULTS: The median follow-up period was 307 days after the anchoring procedure. For the primary outcome, clinical success was achieved in all 5 patients with initial SEMS clinical failure and in all 15 patients overall. The median angle of the SEMS significantly straightened from 128.3° with the initial SEMS alone to 151.5° after anchoring stent placement (p < 0.001). As an exploratory analysis of the 10 patients with early RBO, the m

42416859.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Runway time, defined as the interval between completion of polyethylene glycol ingestion and the start of colonoscopy, has been studied as a determinant of bowel cleansing quality. However, whether the bowel preparation course itself is associated with colonoscope insertion difficulty remains unclear. We aimed to examine the associations of bowel preparation course indicators with cecal intubation time (CIT) and loop formation. METHODS: In this single-center prospective observational study, we enrolled consecutive patients undergoing unsedated colonoscopy and prospectively recorded four bowel preparation course indicators: time to first bowel movement, time to confirmed completion of bowel preparation, total number of bowel movements, and estimated stool volume. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed using log-transformed CIT as the dependent variable and adjusting for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and endoscopist. Associations with loop formation were examined using multivariable logistic regression analysis adjusted for age, BMI, and endoscopist. RESULTS: A total of 185 patients were included. Among the four indicators, only the time to con

42999596.abstract: PURPOSE: Concomitant chemoradiation therapy (cCRT) is a standard-of-care treatment option for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer, improving locoregional control (LRC) and overall survival (OS). However, many patients are unfit for cCRT and receive sequential chemoradiation therapy (sCRT); in this setting, hypofractionated radiation therapy may reduce treatment time, counter tumor repopulation, and improve access. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We retrospectively analyzed outcomes and prognostic factors among 131 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated at a single high-volume cancer center with 1 of 3 approaches: cCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-C; n = 52), sCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-S; n = 37), or sCRT with hypofractionation (HYPO-S; n = 42). RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 19.6 months, OS, progression-free survival, and distant failure-free survival were comparable among groups. LRC was significantly higher with HYPO-S (62.0%) than with CONV-S (34.8%; p = .009) and similar to CONV-C (62.0%). In multivariate analysis, LRC with HYPO-S remained comparable to CONV-C (p = .576), whereas CONV-S was associated with inferior LRC co

42997228.abstract: BACKGROUND: Reduction mammaplasty relieves macromastia symptoms and improves aesthetics. Traditional pedicles offer reliable vascularity for most patients, but their reliability is often limited by resection weight and notch-to-nipple or nipple-to-inframammary fold (N-IMF) distances. The double-unit superomedial central (DUS) pedicle, paired with a vertical resection pattern, was developed to improve vascular reliability and projection across a broader range of patients, irrespective of above mentioned limitations. METHODS: A retrospective review included all consecutive patients undergoing bilateral vertical reduction mammaplasty with the DUS pedicle by a single surgeon at the University of Florida (January 2021-December 2023). Demographic, anatomic, and outcome data were compared between patients with <500 g and ≥500 g resections (based on smaller-breast resection weight) using Welch's t-test and Fisher's exact test. RESULTS: Sixty-three patients (mean age 35.1 ± 16.0 years) were included; most had grade III ptosis (65%) and sternal notch-to-nipple distance ≤37 cm (89%). Thirty-nine patients underwent <500 g resections and 24 underwent ≥500 g resections. Compared with the <500 g

42991498.abstract: Innovation in medical technologies, especially AI-enabled tools, is exposing the limits of Europe's current medical device regulatory dogma. Existing rules treat devices as isolated products rather than integrated systems shaping care. Any region that wants to be home to the most innovative businesses and technologies must have a regulatory system fit for adopting state-of-the-art technologies and making fast, effective decisions. While US and UK frameworks innovate, Europe's model stifles medical-technology innovation and the exploration of new regulatory paradigms through ineffective multi-level governance and uncoordinated, decentralized decision-making. In response, MedTech stakeholders, including industry, professional associations, patient representatives, hospitals, politicians, national authorities, and regulatory scientists, have recently called for a centralised EU-level "single-authority" (for strategy-setting, coordination, and regulatory support) to take accountable ownership of the regulatory system and its strategic development for all medical technologies in Europe. We describe the benefits and drawbacks of this approach and contend how centralization in the complex

42991435.abstract: BACKGROUND: Health systems increasingly deploy predictive and generative artificial intelligence (AI) to improve care delivery and outcomes. Predictive AI models estimate the risk of future events to inform targeted interventions, while generative AI systems extract, summarize, and communicate information and may automate selected tasks. Routine deployment generates clinical, operational, and interaction data that can support evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of AI-enabled workflows. METHODS: We review approaches to generating real-world evidence (RWE) from routine deployment of predictive and generative AI across four implementation configurations: silent deployment, human-in-the-loop (HITL), human-on-the-loop (HOTL), and automated. For each configuration, we describe the evaluation questions, routinely generated data, and feasible study designs. RESULTS: Each implementation configuration supports different forms of evidence about model performance, workflow effectiveness, human oversight, and safety. For both predictive and generative AI, silent deployment supports assessment of local performance and subgroup differences. Once predictive AI drives action, evaluating the

42990880.abstract: PURPOSE: Hydrogel spacers reduce the rectal radiation dose and toxicity in prostate cancer radiation therapy. However, their use in other malignancies, including renal cell carcinoma (RCC), remains underexplored. This study aimed to explore the feasibility of hydrogel spacer placement at different retroperitoneal sites and its potential dosimetric effects during stereotactic body radiation therapy for RCC using cadaveric models. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Hydrogel spacers were percutaneously administered under computed tomography (CT) guidance to 3 cadavers at the following retroperitoneal sites: (1) the perirenal space, (2) the perivascular region of the iliac vessels, and (3) the iliacus muscle region. Spacer stability and separation distance from organs at risk were evaluated using CT images acquired immediately after placement, at 1 week, and at 1 to 2 months. The dosimetric effect was assessed in the perirenal spacer case by comparing radiation treatment plans for a simulated RCC lesion generated before and after spacer placement using a treatment planning system. RESULTS: Hydrogel spacer placement in the perirenal space achieved a stable separation of approximately 1 cm between t

42985619.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linke

42979564.abstract: AIMS: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, contributes to neuronal injury after ischemic stroke. Because our previous cancer-cell screens identified ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase, as a ferroptosis regulator, we investigated whether ATM inhibition protects neural tissue after ischemic stroke and examined determinants of therapeutic response. METHODS: ATM inhibitors, including the brain-penetrant clinical compound AZD1390, were evaluated in cultured cancer and neuronal cells, oxygen-glucose-deprived rat and mouse brain slices, and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion models using multiple inbred and Rabep2-genotype mouse strains. Cell viability, cytotoxicity, lipid peroxidation, ferroptosis-associated markers, infarct volume, and collateral vessel density were assessed. Topical AZD1390 was also tested in mice with impaired collateral networks. RESULTS: ATM inhibition reduced ferroptosis-associated lipid oxidative injury and protected neurons in multiple preclinical stroke models. AZD1390 decreased lipid peroxidation and neuronal death, and reduced infarct volume in B6/J and B6/NJ mice, but not in BALB mice. Treatment efficacy varied among st

42960185.abstract: Digital lymphatic anatomy has been defined largely by cadaveric studies. We evaluated whether photoacoustic lymphangiography (PAL) could depict three-dimensional anatomy and motion-related deformation in vivo. Two healthy volunteers and one patient with secondary upper-extremity lymphedema underwent fingertip indocyanine green injection, near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and static and dynamic PAL. In healthy fingers, lymphatic vessels coursed mainly along the lateral aspects toward the dorsal hand and lay between superficial veins and digital arteries. Flexion produced spiral-like deformation or abrupt angulation, whereas vessels were relatively straight during extension; segmental lymphatic signals moved proximally during motion. In the patient, PAL visualized vessels beneath dermal backflow that appeared more irregular and showed frequent short-segment tortuosity, and guided lymphaticovenular anastomosis. These findings support the feasibility of finger-specific, in vivo three-dimensional and motion-resolved assessment of digital lymphatic morphology using PAL.

42921337.abstract: The two earthquakes that recently struck the northern coast of Venezuela will deepen a health crisis that has troubled the country for twenty years. They have exposed how weak its health infrastructure is, how scarce medicines are, how little epidemiological surveillance remains, and how long investment has been lacking. The humanitarian health crisis in Venezuela did not arise from armed conflict, as it has elsewhere. Its roots lie in decades of authoritarian rule and institutional decay, which have eroded public health capacity, research infrastructure, vaccination coverage and the control of infectious diseases in general. Because these weaknesses have accumulated, the earthquakes may well turn into an even graver humanitarian emergency. Recovery that lasts will not be secured by short-term international aid alone. It will require the rebuilding of accountable institutions able to govern transparently and to apply equitable health policies, so that the health system can regain its resilience.

42909254.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of death worldwide, and their epidemiology is correlated with genetic predisposition and exposure to risk. Brazil is a developing country with a vast territory, which leads to structural inequalities. We aimed to comprehensively characterise the epidemiology and burden of CVD in Brazil between 1996 and 2023, examining temporal trends, regional disparities, demographic patterns, healthcare costs, and heart transplantation. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective descriptive ecological study using aggregated administrative data from the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), Brazil's publicly funded national health system. Mortality, hospitalization, and heart transplantation data from 1996 to 2023 were analysed according to sex, race/ethnicity, age, and geographic region. We estimated mortality rates for the major CVD, hospital length of stay, healthcare expenditures, and heart transplantation activity. FINDINGS: Acute myocardial infarction remained the leading cause of cardiovascular mortality throughout the study period, while hypertensive diseases overtook heart failure after 2016 as the second leading cause

42898116.abstract: Radiation dose to the heart is associated with various cardiac side effects. However, the specific cardiac and pulmonary structures that contribute to these toxicities remain incompletely understood. Moreover, although multiple factors contribute to reduced survival after radiotherapy, the role of radiation-induced cardiac toxicity remains underrecognized. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the associations between radiation dose to specific cardiac and pulmonary structures, cardiac side effects, and survival. A total of 137 clinical studies were analysed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Associations between radiation dose and cardiac side effects were identified not only for the whole heart but also for specific cardiac substructures, including myocardial segments, coronary arteries, and the pericardium. Notably, radiation dose to the lungs was also associated with decline in cardiac function, suggesting that minimizing cardiac toxicity may require consideration of both local cardiac irradiation and non-local irradiation of adjacent organs, particularly the lungs. Direct evidence linking cardiac side effects to survival was limited. Nevertheless, the observed associati

42898053.abstract: The Brief Assessment of Cognition in Schizophrenia (BACS) and its Japanese version are widely used instruments for the brief and efficient assessment of cognitive domains commonly impaired in schizophrenia. A tablet-administered version, the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) App, has been developed; however, normative data for the BAC App have not yet been established for the general Japanese population. This cross-sectional study aimed to establish normative data for the Japanese version of the BAC App in healthy Japanese individuals. A total of 120 participants aged 12-69 years were recruited, with 10 male and 10 female participants in each of six age groups. Cognitive performance was assessed using BAC App subtests, and mean scores and standard deviations were calculated for each age- and sex-defined subgroup. Most subtests showed stable performance distributions across age groups. No notable differences between forms were observed for the Tower of London Task. In contrast, a substantial difference between forms was observed for the Verbal Memory Task, with higher recall performance for Form 3. Structural characteristics of the word lists may contribute to form-dependent diffe

42833407.abstract: BACKGROUND: Generative AI chatbots are increasingly used for emotional support, yet their safety remains insufficiently characterized across repeated interactions. Prior work relied mostly on single-session prompts, limiting evaluation of changes in responses across days. The present study aimed to assess how major AI chatbots respond to escalating suicidal risk over time, including imminent-risk scenarios and attempts to bypass safeguards (jailbreaking). METHODS: We simulated interactions with ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Replika across three suicidal risk scenarios with risk escalation over seven days, informed by the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale. Outcomes included exploration of suicidal ideation, symptom assessment, referral to human support, and vulnerability to jailbreak attempts. RESULTS: In ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Replika, respectively, overall human referral occurred in 54/63 (85.7%), 48/63 (76.2%), and 6/63 (9.5%) daily records. During the high-risk period, exploration of suicidal ideation was higher for ChatGPT than DeepSeek (adjusted difference, 25.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 2.4-49.5; q = 0.037) and Replika (66.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 44.2-89.1; q < 0.001). 42828106.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate clinical outcomes and toxicity of definitive interstitial or hybrid interventional radiotherapy (IRT; brachytherapy) using high-dose-rate (HDR) or pulsed-dose-rate (PDR) techniques for non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) unsuitable for standard superficial treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center analysis included 49 patients with 50 histologically confirmed basal cell carcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma lesions treated between October 2020 and December 2023. Primary and recurrent lesions treated with definitive HDR- or PDR-based interstitial or hybrid IRT were included. Local control, acute reactions, late effects, and dosimetric parameters were assessed. Adverse events were graded according to Radiation Therapy Oncology Group criteria. RESULTS: Basal cell carcinoma accounted for 37 lesions and squamous cell carcinoma for 13. Twenty-eight lesions were primary tumors and 22 were recurrences after surgery. Interstitial IRT alone was used in 35 lesions and hybrid IRT in 15; 30 lesions received HDR-IRT and 20 received PDR-IRT. Median follow-up was 21.2 months. Local control was achieved in 47 of 50 lesions (94%), and the estimated 2-year loc

42825134.abstract: Distal phalangeal nonunion is a rare but challenging condition that may result from crush injuries or inadequate stabilization. Surgical fixation is often difficult because of the small size of the fragment and surrounding soft tissue damage. We report two cases of symptomatic distal phalanx nonunion successfully treated with autologous bone peg grafting. The first case involved a 13-year-old boy who developed nonunion following a bicycle injury. The second case involved a 31-year-old man who sustained an open fracture in a workplace accident. In both cases, a cortical bone peg harvested from the posterior aspect of the ipsilateral proximal ulna was inserted into the medullary canal of the distal phalanx to provide mechanical stability and promote bone healing. Radiographic union was achieved within 3 months, and both patients returned to full activity, with one experiencing minor residual symptoms.

42822184.abstract: Psychiatric disorders, such as schizophrenia and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), are associated with altered functional connectivity (FC) and are often accompanied by cognitive deficits. Leveraging the shared neural mechanisms underlying both psychiatric disorders and cognitive impairment may improve diagnostic accuracy. However, due to the complexity and heterogeneity of these conditions, diagnosis based on FC alone remains challenging in terms of accuracy and biomarker reliability. To address these challenges, we propose a meta-analysis prompt guided multi-task graph transformer network that simultaneously predicts psychiatric disorder and cognitive deficits while identifying associated alterations in brain FC. The proposed framework employs a graph transformer as a common encoder and integrates a joint attention mechanism to capture shared disorder-cognition representations, together with saliency pooling to identify task-relevant brain regions. To enhance the robustness and interpretability of the learned saliency patterns, we introduce large language models (LLMs) to encode meta-analysis priors derived from the BrainMap database. Specifically, activation proba

42815423.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Neonatal jaundice remains a major health challenge, particularly in resource-limited environments where reliable diagnosis is not readily accessible. While image-based and AI-driven approaches have demonstrated encouraging diagnostic performance, their limited generalizability across different datasets, populations, and clinical settings remains a major challenge. METHODS: This study proposes a Dual-Teacher Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation (DT-CMKD) framework for efficient neonatal jaundice diagnosis. Complementary knowledge is distilled from two teachers: a vision-based MambaVision model capturing rich spatial features from neonatal images and a text-based model combining multimodal LLaMA-3-17B and CLIP ViT-B/32 text encoder to generate semantic embeddings from clinically informed neonatal image descriptions. The distilled knowledge from both teachers is transferred to a lightweight ResNet-50 student via multi-level distillation integrating logit-based supervision, feature alignment, and cross-entropy optimization. RESULTS: The proposed model was trained and validated on the Normal and Jaundiced Newborn (NJN) dataset. Further, we introduce JaundiSet-NG

42800955.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown high capabilities in several software development-related tasks such as program repair, documentation, code refactoring, debugging, and testing. However, training these models requires massive amount of data and significant computational resources. Adapters are specialized, small modules designed for parameter efficient fine-tuning of LLMs for specific tasks, domains, or applications without requiring extensive retraining of the entire model. These adapters offer a more efficient way to customize LLMs for particular needs, leveraging the pre-existing capabilities of the large model. Model (and adapter) merging have emerged as a technique to develop one model capable of multiple tasks, with minimal or no training required. Although model and adapter merging has shown promising performance in domains such as natural language processing and computer vision, its applicability to software engineering tasks remains underexplored. In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of merged adapters within the context of software engineering, with a particular focus on the Automated Program Repair (APR) task, through our approach, MergeRepair. In parti

42787771.abstract: PURPOSE: Acute radiotherapy is essential in oncological emergencies, but delays may occur before or after referral to radiation oncology. The primary aim of this study was to characterize timing intervals in a tertiary supraregional care network. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre analysis included patients treated with acute radiotherapy for urgent tumour-related symptoms at our department between 2009 and 2024. Timing intervals from symptom onset to presentation and from presentation to radiotherapy start were analyzed. Referral patterns and weekday distribution were secondary organisational outcomes; symptomatic response and survival were assessed descriptively. All comparative analyses were exploratory and unadjusted. RESULTS: Overall, 314 patients treated at 349 treatment sites were included. The most frequent indication was metastatic spinal cord compression-related symptoms (260/349; 74.5%). 45.8% of all treatment sites were referred from external institutions. Median time from symptom onset to presentation was 5 days (IQR 2-16.25), whereas median time from presentation to radiotherapy start was 0 days (IQR 0-1).
